global.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex
global.summary: Purpose-built hardened infrastructure makes this one of the most defensible options on the board.

global.name: Andaman Islands
global.summary: The Andamans are one of the strongest long-horizon options: maritime isolation and resource diversity create resilience if governance and inter-island logistics stay coherent.

global.name: Mont Saint-Michel
global.summary: Mont Saint-Michel is one of the hardest micro-sites to assault thanks to tidal separation; what kills you here is throughput limits in food, space, and medical response.

global.name: Isle of Eigg Village
global.summary: Eigg is a rare island community with real off-grid credibility; what kills you here is a bad season that breaks food, fuel, and medical margins before security fails.

global.name: Tasmania
global.summary: Tasmania is one of the strongest balanced options: durable food-water-energy potential with enough separation to reduce pressure.

global.name: Chiloé Island
global.summary: Chiloé is a strong all-round island base with workable agriculture and defensible approaches, but what kills you here is prolonged maritime cutoff during a hard winter.

global.name: Cusco Highlands Village
global.summary: Cusco highlands villages combine terrain defense with proven local subsistence systems, but what kills you here is cold-altitude medical decline in unacclimated groups.

global.name: Heligoland
global.summary: Heligoland is one of the strongest isolation plays in Western Europe: remote, compact, and easier to monitor than mainland sites. What kills you here is maritime dependency when weather or fuel cuts the lifeline.

global.name: Seychelles
global.summary: Seychelles is one of the strongest African macro-base options because exceptional island isolation combines with a livable climate and realistic long-term habitation potential. The main constraint is coordination and resupply across dispersed islands once external systems weaken.

global.name: Mehrangarh Fort
global.summary: Mehrangarh combines exceptional fortification geometry with workable internal scale, making it one of the stronger fortress options if surrounding pressure is actively managed.

global.name: Machu Picchu
global.summary: Machu Picchu offers excellent terrain defense and controlled approach lines, but limited productive capacity prevents large, permanent survival communities.

global.name: Simien Mountains
global.summary: The Simien Mountains are a naturally defensible high-altitude stronghold, where sheer cliffs, limited access routes, and extreme isolation significantly reduce external threat pressure. However, that same isolation severely limits long-term survivability, with constrained food production, harsh living conditions, and difficult resupply. Over time, the balance shifts from protection to restriction, making it better suited to short-term refuge than permanent settlement.

global.name: Carcassonne
global.summary: Carcassonne is a premier fortified shell with layered walls and command depth; what kills you here is sustainment fatigue behind intact defenses.

global.name: Faroe Islands
global.summary: Faroe is one of Europe's strongest isolation plays, but what kills you here is maritime bottleneck failure when storms, fuel limits, and fleet wear cut food and medical imports.

global.name: Hilltop Fort Rajasthan
global.summary: A Rajasthan hill fort is a classic high-control stronghold with excellent wall geometry, but water and heat stress define whether it thrives or slowly fails.

global.name: Socotra Island
global.summary: Socotra gives outstanding separation from collapse corridors, but what kills you here is maritime supply fracture: once sea links fail, medicine, tools, and replacement goods run out faster than local systems can adapt.

global.name: Fiji Islands
global.summary: Fiji balances isolation and livability better than most island options, but cyclone and maritime dependence cap reliability.

global.name: Krak des Chevaliers
global.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a premier fortress for holding ground, but what kills you here is siege economics: ammunition, medicine, and calories run out long before the walls meaningfully fail.

global.name: Palawan
global.summary: Palawan is a large island system that balances isolation, defensibility, and resource diversity. It works when distributed settlements and logistics are coordinated at island-wide scale. You die when governance fractures and shipping disruption desynchronizes regional supply.

global.name: Kodiak Island
global.summary: Kodiak is a high-isolation island with credible wild-resource potential, but its dominant failure mode is climate-logistics attrition: severe weather and seasonal bottlenecks steadily erode throughput, maintenance, and medical resilience.

global.name: Matmata Underground Dwellings
global.summary: Matmata offers a strong concealment-defense package with naturally insulated subterranean housing and manageable access points. Its core trade-off is protected living space versus limited scale and external dependence for growth.

global.name: Rice Terrace Highlands
global.summary: Rice Terrace Highlands are elevated agrarian settlements with built-in food potential. They work by combining controllable approach routes with reliable staple production systems. You die when irrigation, labor coordination, or slope access fails during stress cycles.

global.name: Sigiriya
global.summary: Sigiriya offers rare rock-fortress defensibility and visibility, but constrained top-plateau capacity limits how long a group can live there without strong external support.

global.name: Zanzibar Island
global.summary: Zanzibar balances meaningful island separation with established settlement infrastructure, making it a credible medium-to-long-term refuge if governance and resource management remain coherent. Its challenge is that it is populated and close enough to mainland dynamics to face persistent pressure.

global.name: Burlington Bunker
global.summary: Burlington is exceptionally hard to breach in the opening phase; what kills you here is closed-system decay once consumables, maintenance, or governance slip.

global.name: Cappadocia Highlands
global.summary: Cappadocia’s broken terrain and concealment options make it a strong defensive refuge, but what kills you here is water-and-agriculture throughput: dispersed hideouts can outlast attacks, not prolonged scarcity.

global.name: Coober Pedy Underground Settlement
global.summary: Coober Pedy is one of the few desert sites where underground habitation is already proven, but long-term success is limited by hard water and logistics ceilings.

global.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
global.summary: Derinkuyu is an elite hide-and-hold refuge, but what kills you here is subterranean throughput collapse: ventilation, waste handling, and calorie flow fail before defenses do.

global.name: Gotland
global.summary: Gotland is a robust island option with workable infrastructure, but what kills you here is coastline overextension: too many access points for too few defenders over time.

global.name: Hanle Observatory
global.summary: Hanle Observatory is an isolation-dominant survival option with low encounter pressure, but extreme altitude and remoteness impose severe physiological and logistics penalties.

global.name: Jeju Island
global.summary: Jeju is a strong island refuge with usable farmland, water access, and natural maritime separation from mainland spillover. What kills you here is maritime choke failure: if ports and fuel fail, an island-scale population can out-consume local capacity.

global.name: Kargil War Bunkers
global.summary: Kargil War Bunkers are military-hardened high-altitude positions designed to resist assault. They work by combining strong fortification with terrain that channels approaches. You die when cold-weather fuel, medical, and resupply throughput collapses before defenses do.

global.name: Mount Huashan
global.summary: Mount Huashan is an elite defensive perch with severe access control and strong natural isolation. The decisive trade-off is near-unmatched protection versus chronic logistical fragility.

global.name: Siwa Oasis
global.summary: Siwa Oasis is one of the more credible long-horizon refuges in the region, but what kills you here is water-system fragility: contamination, overdraw, or pump failure can collapse the settlement’s carrying capacity.

global.name: 2e REP Barracks (Calvi)
global.summary: 2e REP Calvi is a hard military compound with disciplined layout and perimeter control, but it sits on a populated island with finite local capacity. What kills you here is prolonged resupply failure after the initial defensive advantage burns off.

global.name: Aït Benhaddou
global.summary: Aït Benhaddou is a strong niche base: its fortified settlement form and relative isolation support controlled defense and lower immediate pressure. Its long-term ceiling is set by arid constraints, where limited water and food capacity become the decisive bottleneck.

global.name: Galápagos Islands
global.summary: Galápagos has extreme isolation and low random threat traffic, but what kills you here is supply collapse once imported essentials stop.

global.name: Great Wall Fortress Sections
global.summary: Great Wall fortress sections provide strong engineered defense lines and terrain leverage, but they are fragmented assets rather than turnkey settlements. The dominant trade-off is excellent barrier control versus poor self-sustaining living capacity.

global.name: Hallstatt
global.summary: Hallstatt combines constrained access with strong local livability, making it one of the better balanced settlement options. What kills you here is chokepoint failure that traps residents against terrain.

global.name: Iwo Jima Underground Bunkers
global.summary: Iwo Jima’s bunker network is exceptionally hard to assault and highly isolated, but it is austere and resource-poor. What kills you here is life-support collapse underground: water, ventilation, and medical limits outrun defensive advantages.

global.name: Malbork Castle
global.summary: Malbork provides exceptional masonry defense and layered gates, but it sits in a reachable lowland region. What kills you here is siege attrition: repeated encirclement and supply disruption grind down even a strong fortress.

global.name: Telluride
global.summary: Mountain terrain and manageable scale make Telluride a credible holdout if you prepare for winter logistics.

global.name: Titan Missile Museum (Silo 571-7)
global.summary: A tough underground shell with real protective value, but limited habitability without major adaptation.

global.name: Visby
global.summary: Visby is a balanced walled island town, but what kills you here is population-and-water strain if too many survivors concentrate behind finite historic defenses.

global.name: Île d’Yeu
global.summary: Île d’Yeu is a balanced island refuge with useful separation and livable conditions, but it lacks deep strategic depth. What kills you here is slow resource depletion under prolonged isolation.

global.name: Area 51
global.summary: Area 51 combines remoteness, controlled approaches, and hardened infrastructure, but its dominant failure mode is systems complexity debt: without specialized maintenance pipelines, high-tech capabilities decay into unusable overhead.

global.name: Fasil Ghebbi
global.summary: Fasil Ghebbi is a fortified royal compound with thick masonry, layered courtyards, and strong internal control, giving it above-average defensive potential in an inland setting. It is more balanced than many heritage landmarks, but long-term survival still depends on building reliable food, water, and medical systems beyond the walls.

global.name: Lindisfarne
global.summary: A tidal island with natural separation, limited access windows, and a defensible settlement pattern. It works well for a disciplined small group, but tide dependency and resource limits cap long-term resilience.

global.name: Predjama Castle
global.summary: Predjama is a superb cliff fortress with choke-point control, but fortress geometry does not make food or medicine. What kills you here is siege starvation: you can deny entry for a long time and still lose to depletion.

global.name: Qeshm Island
global.summary: Qeshm offers valuable island separation and room for mixed subsistence, but what kills you here is control dilution: the island is large enough that fragmented authority invites persistent infiltration and internal conflict.

global.name: RAAF Base Tindal
global.summary: High-grade military infrastructure gives strong initial control, but strategic visibility and supply dependence limit endurance.

global.name: Rocamadour
global.summary: Rocamadour balances cliffside defense with workable rural linkage; what kills you here is exceeding carrying capacity and overloading water/sanitation systems.

global.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge Cliffs
global.summary: Tiger Leaping Gorge offers extraordinary terrain defense and low approach density, but daily survival is constrained by space and supply movement. The central trade-off is tactical dominance versus unworkable sustainment at scale.

global.name: Tiger’s Nest Monastery
global.summary: Tiger’s Nest is an extreme cliffside redoubt with elite access denial, but its tiny carrying capacity and severe logistics ceiling cap long-term survival.

global.name: Alcatraz Island
global.summary: Alcatraz buys strong early security through water separation and choke-point access, but the decisive failure mode is supply starvation: once boat fuel, food inflow, and repair parts lapse, the island becomes a sealed deficit zone.

global.name: Anna Creek Station
global.summary: Exceptional scale and remoteness support long-run survival potential, but the footprint is too vast to secure conventionally.

global.name: Banda Neira
global.summary: A small island settlement with strong maritime separation, historic fortifications, and access to coastal resources. It works best as a low-profile island refuge, but limited scale and supply dependence cap long-term resilience.

global.name: Caerphilly Castle
global.summary: A large moated castle with strong defensive design and layered barriers. It is one of the stronger historic fortifications, but modern exposure and limited self-sufficiency keep it from elite status.

global.name: Greenland
global.summary: A vast Arctic island with extreme isolation, natural resources, and scattered settlements. However, harsh climate, huge scale, and infrastructure dependency make it difficult to control or sustain.

global.name: Himeji Castle
global.summary: Himeji Castle delivers high-quality fortress geometry and controlled internal defense, but its urban context limits long-term security. The key trade-off is superb structure versus low isolation.

global.name: Itaipu Dam
global.summary: Itaipu Dam has exceptional energy potential and water access, making it operationally powerful, but its scale and strategic value make defense extremely demanding.

global.name: Masada
global.summary: Masada is brutally hard to assault, but what kills you here is plateau logistics: water, heat management, and medical throughput collapse before attackers can force entry.

global.name: Mesa Verde
global.summary: Mesa Verde offers strong terrain defense, but what kills you here is carrying-capacity mismatch: protected positions can hold people, yet arable throughput and water logistics limit long-run population support.

global.name: Olavsvern Naval Base
global.summary: A hardened underground naval base with strong concealment and protected infrastructure. However, confined systems, external supply needs, and limited scalability restrict long-term survival.

global.name: St Kilda
global.summary: An extremely remote island archipelago with exceptional isolation and low external threat pressure. Its weakness is sustainment: weather, landing difficulty, and limited resources make survival fragile over time.

global.name: Nagurskoye Air Base
global.summary: A remote Arctic military airbase with controlled access and strong strategic positioning. However, extreme climate, visibility, and dependence on supply chains reduce independent survivability.

global.name: Vancouver Island
global.summary: Vancouver Island is one of the most balanced large-island options, but its dominant failure mode is population-interface pressure: connected urban corridors and ferry chokepoints can overwhelm otherwise strong local resources.

global.name: Camp Lemonnier
global.summary: Camp Lemonnier has exceptional military-grade defensive capability and organized base infrastructure, making it one of the strongest compounds in a direct security sense. But it is not highly independent: if fuel, water treatment, and logistics pipelines fail, performance drops fast.

global.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
global.summary: A purpose-built tunnel network with concealment, restricted access, and strong defensive history. It is highly effective for short-term evasion, but confinement, ventilation, and resource limits make permanent survival difficult.

global.name: Fort George
global.summary: A purpose-built coastal military fort with strong walls, controlled access, and organised internal space. It has real defensive value, but exposure and reliance on external supplies limit long-term independence.

global.name: Fort Jefferson
global.summary: Fort Jefferson is an exceptional sea-fortress with clear defensive geometry and extreme stand-off distance, but its dominant failure mode is water-energy fragility: if desalination and fuel chains degrade, habitability collapses quickly.

global.name: HM Prison Dartmoor
global.summary: A remote prison complex with secure walls, controlled movement, and strong internal containment. It offers a credible short-term defensive shell, but harsh exposure and limited self-sufficiency constrain long-term survival.

global.name: Ha Long Bay Cliffs
global.summary: Ha Long Bay cliffs are a terrain-fragmented coastal redoubt of islands and vertical rock. It works by forcing movement through predictable maritime channels and narrow landing points. You die when weather or boat degradation cuts mobility and resupply between sectors.

global.name: Hue Citadel
global.summary: Hue Citadel is a fortified urban compound with layered walls and controlled gates. It works as a short-to-medium defensive enclave where geometry slows penetration. You die when siege pressure outlasts external food, fuel, and medical inflows.

global.name: Maori Pa Fortifications
global.summary: Strong terrain-first fortifications can stop early incursions, but most pa sites fail once stocks and water run thin.

global.name: Pathankot Air Force Station
global.summary: Pathankot AFS is a hardened operational compound with meaningful defensive structure, but its strategic visibility keeps pressure high and long-term autonomy uncertain.

global.name: Suomenlinna Fortress
global.summary: Suomenlinna has real island-fortress defensive logic, but it is tied to nearby urban waters and maritime supply. What kills you here is blockade-driven depletion when fuel, food, and treatment capacity cannot be replenished.

global.name: Clovelly
global.summary: A steep coastal village with constrained access routes, natural defensibility, and small-scale shelter. It is viable as a compact refuge, but limited expansion, coastal exposure, and supply dependence restrict long-term survival.

global.name: Edinburgh Castle
global.summary: A highly defensible urban castle on elevated rock, with strong visibility and controlled approaches. It is excellent as a symbolic redoubt, but urban exposure and limited sustainability reduce long-term value.

global.name: Kibber Village
global.summary: Kibber is a high-altitude remote village that trades accessibility for security. It works through isolation, narrow approaches, and existing community housing for organized routines. You die when winter isolation, fuel gaps, or delayed medical care compound faster than recovery.

global.name: Komodo Island
global.summary: Komodo is a highly isolated island refuge with strong separation from mainland pressure. It works by limiting approach routes and maintaining disciplined low-population maritime living. You die when freshwater constraints and sea-logistics disruption trigger cascading shortages.

global.name: Lakshadweep
global.summary: Lakshadweep is a distributed island-chain refuge where sea separation reduces routine contact and gives strong early warning. It works when multiple islands coordinate boats, storage, and rationing as one system. You die when maritime links or freshwater discipline fail and each island is stranded alone.

global.name: McMurdo Station
global.summary: A large Antarctic research station with infrastructure, shelter, and operational capacity. However, harsh conditions and dependence on supply chains limit true long-term independence.

global.name: Table Mountain Plateau
global.summary: Table Mountain Plateau is a highly defensible elevated position with steep cliffs, strong visibility, and usable space on top. However, its direct proximity to Cape Town, multiple access routes, and high visibility make it far less secure than more remote mountain strongholds. It is better suited to short-term defence and staging than long-term isolation.

global.name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
global.summary: An extremely isolated scientific station with controlled infrastructure and almost no external threat pressure. However, total dependence on life-support systems and resupply makes long-term independence impossible.

global.name: Longyearbyen
global.summary: A remote Arctic settlement with strong isolation, infrastructure, and controlled access. However, extreme climate and supply-chain reliance constrain long-term resilience.

global.name: Petra
global.summary: Petra offers strong chokepoints and concealment in stone corridors, but what kills you here is water dependency: once stored supply and nearby sources are contested, defensive geometry cannot feed or hydrate a population.

global.name: San Felipe Fortress
global.summary: San Felipe combines historical fortification advantages with moderate operating feasibility, but limited local throughput caps long-term resilience.

global.name: Vietnam Tunnel Systems
global.summary: A broader tunnel-system concept with strong concealment and movement control across difficult terrain. It provides tactical advantage, but fragmented infrastructure and poor long-term livability keep it below true stronghold status.

global.name: Danum Valley Field Centre
global.summary: Danum Valley Field Centre is a remote jungle refuge with low-contact signature advantages. It works for small trained groups that can run strict field medicine and maintenance routines. You die when treatable illness, injury, or equipment failure outpaces evacuation and repair.

global.name: Murmansk Icebreaker Port
global.summary: A polar maritime hub with specialist icebreaker infrastructure and Arctic access. However, port exposure, supply dependency, and harsh operating conditions limit long-term security.

global.name: Pine Gap Facility
global.summary: Extreme remoteness and hardened controls are offset by acute system dependency and top-tier strategic exposure.

global.name: Al Udeid Air Base
global.summary: Al Udeid provides one of the best ready-made defense envelopes in the region, but what kills you here is signature load: major airbase visibility attracts sustained external pressure and drains supplies.

global.name: Antarctic Peninsula
global.summary: A remote polar region with natural isolation and access to coastal landing points. However, severe weather, limited infrastructure, and scarce sustainable resources make survival highly fragile.

global.name: Elmina Castle
global.summary: Elmina Castle is a heavily fortified coastal stronghold with thick walls, controlled internal spaces, and clear defensive advantages. However, its position within a populated coastal town and direct access from land and sea significantly reduce its long-term viability, making it better suited to temporary defence than sustained survival.

global.name: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base
global.summary: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base is a military command compound with strong tactical security. It works through hardened access control, organized response, and maritime support infrastructure. You die when prolonged contest burns fuel, parts, and readiness faster than resupply.

global.name: Okinawa
global.summary: Okinawa offers meaningful island separation and workable living conditions, but dense infrastructure and strategic visibility increase contest pressure. What kills you here is competition over ports, fuel, and transport hubs that fractures island stability.

global.name: Amazon Tall Tower Observatory
global.summary: ATTO offers deep-rainforest isolation and strong natural resource potential, but terrain, disease burden, and mobility constraints make control and continuity difficult.

global.name: Banlung
global.summary: A remote inland town with surrounding terrain, forest cover, and regional resource access. It offers more livability than a pure wilderness refuge, but weak defensibility and difficult logistics limit its ceiling.

global.name: Bonny Island LNG Terminal
global.summary: Bonny LNG Terminal is a powerful industrial strongpoint with controlled space and hard infrastructure, but it is brittle under collapse conditions. Its usefulness depends on complex systems, skilled maintenance, and steady supply chains that are hard to replace locally.

global.name: Guantanamo Bay
global.summary: Guantanamo offers strong perimeter control and organized facilities, yet the dominant failure mode is geopolitical encirclement: prolonged dependence on maritime logistics and contested sovereignty can choke continuity even before direct breach.

global.name: Porton Down
global.summary: A secure research facility with controlled access, specialist infrastructure, and perimeter discipline. It has defensive value, but technical dependency, contamination risk, and strategic visibility create serious long-term weakness.

global.name: Sime Darby Palm Oil Estate (Sabah)
global.summary: Sime Darby Sabah is a large agro-industrial estate that can produce at regional scale. It works when core zones, mills, roads, and workforce discipline stay synchronized. You die when security overstretch and machinery dependence cause cascading output loss.

global.name: Table Rock Plateau
global.summary: Table Rock is a serviceable elevated fallback, but what kills you here is perimeter dilution: broad approach arcs and limited concealment stretch defenders until incidents become constant.

global.name: Beijing Underground City
global.summary: Beijing Underground City is hard to clear and hard to spot, but it is still a buried extension of a megacity. What kills you here is ventilation and water-system failure once surface utilities, filters, and spare parts stop flowing.

global.name: Blue Mountains Cliffs
global.summary: Excellent terrain defense and standoff distance, with sustainment limited by wildfire and infrastructure thinness.

global.name: Kimberley Big Hole & Mining Complex
global.summary: The Kimberley Big Hole offers strong terrain-based defensibility, but it is a dangerous bowl if exits, water access, or supply routes fail. It works as a hard-to-storm holdout early on, yet can quickly become a trap once core lifelines are cut.

global.name: Maginot Line Bunkers
global.summary: The Maginot bunkers are elite for hard protection but poor at independent endurance. What kills you here is subsystem failure underground: air, water, power, and sanitation.

global.name: NATO Airbase Geilenkirchen
global.summary: Geilenkirchen offers serious NATO-grade infrastructure and layered security, but it is embedded in dense mainland networks. What kills you here is constant contact pressure once perimeter staffing and logistics slip.

global.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
global.summary: Neuschwanstein offers strong terrain-assisted defense and visibility; what kills you here is logistics drag from a symbolic site that cannot feed itself.

global.name: Patagonian Village
global.summary: Patagonian villages benefit from remoteness and low traffic, but what kills you here is wind-cold exposure when fuel and shelter maintenance fall behind.

global.name: Shirakawa-go
global.summary: Shirakawa-go benefits from mountain remoteness and small-settlement cohesion, but severe winters and limited redundancy constrain endurance. What kills you here is winter logistics failure: heat, medicine, and mobility collapse before threats do.

global.name: Tambopata Research Center
global.summary: Tambopata gives concealment and food potential in deep jungle, but what kills you here is untreated injury or infection far from reliable care.

global.name: Hutchinson Salt Storage Caverns
global.summary: Hutchinson salt caverns provide excellent blast/weather protection and concealment, yet the single dominant failure mode is ventilation-power dependency: lose airflow and pumping reliability, and the underground advantage becomes a liability.

global.name: Port Vila
global.summary: Port Vila offers real settlement infrastructure and island separation, but limited depth makes it fragile under prolonged disruption.

global.name: Singapore Port
global.summary: A globally significant port with exceptional logistics, maritime access, and infrastructure. Those strengths become liabilities in collapse, as exposure, density, and strategic importance make it almost impossible to hold.

global.name: The Roaches
global.summary: A rocky elevated ridge with natural defensibility, visibility, and difficult approaches. It works as a temporary fallback point, but exposure and lack of infrastructure make it unsuitable for long-term occupation.

global.name: Wadi Musa
global.summary: Wadi Musa is workable but fragile; what kills you here is corridor squeeze: limited approach routes become contested chokepoints that choke trade, movement, and medical evacuation.

global.name: Bangkok Airport
global.summary: A major transport hub with huge space, supplies, and infrastructure. It fails as a base because urban proximity, scale, and uncontrolled entry points make it impossible to secure.

global.name: Camp Century Ice Tunnels
global.summary: Camp Century is exceptionally hard to reach and hard to assault, but it fails as a settlement because the environment itself destroys long-term habitability.

global.name: Norilsk
global.summary: Norilsk is remote enough to avoid mass contact, but the environment itself is hostile to human endurance. What kills you here is infrastructure-coupled cold exposure: once heat, shelter integrity, or medical capability slip, mortality spikes fast.

global.name: Olenya Air Base
global.summary: Olenya can absorb early shock thanks to military-grade hardening and Arctic distance, but what kills you here is fuel-and-spares collapse in extreme cold once central logistics break.

global.name: Ras Al Khair Desalination Plant
global.summary: Ras Al Khair’s water output is uniquely valuable, but what kills you here is power-chain fragility: once energy input or specialist maintenance fails, the core survival advantage disappears fast.

global.name: Shaxi Ancient Town
global.summary: Shaxi is a remote town with manageable scale and decent local living potential, but it lacks hard defensive geometry. What kills you here is slow attrition from repeated incursions that drain manpower and stores.

global.name: Waw an Namus Cave System
global.summary: Waw an Namus is one of the hardest places to reach, which dramatically lowers threat pressure. The same isolation becomes the fatal weakness because survival systems are almost entirely import-dependent.

global.name: Ajanta Caves
global.summary: Ajanta Caves are a hardened cave shelter system with strong choke-point defense. It works for short protected occupancy because rock-cut access geometry lowers breach risk. You die when confinement-driven sanitation and resource limits outrun defensive advantages.

global.name: Amazon BHX4 Fulfilment Centre
global.summary: A huge logistics warehouse with stored goods, space, and controlled internal areas. It gives a strong early advantage, but weak defensibility, dependence on systems, and surrounding access routes make it decay quickly.

global.name: Crevasse Field Glacier
global.summary: A fractured glacial terrain filled with deep crevasses, offering extreme isolation and natural barriers. However, unstable footing, concealed crevasse risk, and lack of resources make long-term survival nearly impossible.

global.name: Kuttanad Village
global.summary: Kuttanad is a food-producing lowland basin built around paddy and waterways. It works as a production engine when flood control, storage, and transport are tightly managed. You die when flooding and disease pressure break perimeter control and erase surplus.

global.name: Ryongsong Residence Compound
global.summary: Ryongsong Compound has strong perimeter control and internal zoning, but it remains a politically obvious fixed site in an urban state core. What kills you here is siege pressure once external support and movement options collapse.

global.name: Kolmanskop
global.summary: Kolmanskop buys time through remoteness and clear sightlines, but it cannot feed or hydrate a group for long. The dominant trade-off is safety from people versus total dependence on imported water and food.

global.name: Ligatne Bunker
global.summary: Ligatne's bunker geometry is excellent for sheltering, but what kills you here is air-power-water dependency: once life-support systems degrade, underground becomes a coffin.

global.name: Port Talbot Steelworks
global.summary: A major industrial site with infrastructure, materials, and repair potential. It is useful as a resource node, but pollution, exposure, and system dependency make it weak as a secure living base.

global.name: Foxconn Shenzhen Factory
global.summary: The Shenzhen factory complex has unusual infrastructure depth and short-term resource potential, but it sits inside one of the world’s densest urban-industrial corridors. The dominant trade-off is internal capability versus catastrophic exposure.

global.name: Gdańsk Shipyard
global.summary: Gdańsk Shipyard is a high-value industrial toolkit, not a survivable sanctuary. What kills you here is perimeter overstretch: too much open infrastructure to guard, too many approach paths, too many competing groups.

global.name: Lighthouse Hormuz
global.summary: Hormuz lighthouse has useful separation and surveillance value, but what kills you here is capacity exhaustion: the site is too small and too harsh to sustain a community once short-term stores are depleted.

global.name: Cheddar Gorge Caves
global.summary: Cheddar Gorge caves are a solid tactical hide with useful terrain friction; what kills you here is chronic livability failure, not direct assault.

global.name: Fort Copacabana
global.summary: Copacabana Fort is structurally robust and tactically defensible at the site level, but dense urban surroundings overwhelm long-term survivability.

global.name: UN Base in Juba (UNMISS HQ, South Sudan)
global.summary: UNMISS Juba provides a protected compound that can absorb early shocks, but prolonged crisis drives mounting population pressure into and around the site. Over time, crowding and aid dependence overwhelm what the perimeter can realistically sustain.

global.name: Chernobyl Exclusion Zone Facility
global.summary: Chernobyl offers rare low-population isolation in Europe, but contamination and decaying infrastructure impose a slow-burn survival tax. What kills you here is cumulative exposure and medical degradation, not immediate assault.

global.name: Phu Quoc Lighthouse
global.summary: A coastal lighthouse with visibility, limited access, and some island separation. It offers short-term observation value, but exposure, lack of resources, and dependence on nearby settlement make it weak as a base.

global.name: Cape Point Lighthouse
global.summary: Cape Point Lighthouse has tactical lookout value and some geographic separation, but it lacks the carrying capacity and resource depth needed for sustained habitation. It works best as an observation and signaling outpost rather than a primary survival settlement.

global.name: Fastnet Lighthouse
global.summary: A remote offshore lighthouse with extreme separation and strong visibility. It is nearly useless as a survival base because space, shelter, food, water, and evacuation options are all critically limited.

global.name: KRBL Rice Mill (Dhuri)
global.summary: KRBL Dhuri has serious food-processing upside, but as a fixed base it is exposed, labor-dependent, and hard to secure against persistent pressure.

global.name: La Rinconada
global.summary: La Rinconada gains protection from altitude and remoteness, but extreme living conditions and weak local systems limit survival duration.

global.name: Ruhr Industrial Complex
global.summary: The Ruhr offers broad industrial depth across many nodes; what kills you here is security sprawl that outgrows coordination capacity.

global.name: Antarctic Lighthouse
global.summary: A small polar outpost with visibility and isolation. However, exposure, limited shelter, and lack of resources make it unsuitable for long-term survival.

global.name: Eguisheim
global.summary: Eguisheim is a workable village-scale fallback with manageable density and access to surrounding land. What kills you here is perimeter dilution once pressure exceeds what a small settlement can police.

global.name: Fort Denison
global.summary: A compact fortified island position with controllable access but almost no independent sustainment depth.

global.name: Naours Underground City
global.summary: Naours gives useful subterranean concealment and controlled entry, but it was never built as a full independent city. What kills you here is prolonged underground strain: air quality, hygiene, and supply depletion.

global.name: Potosí Silver Mine (Cerro Rico)
global.summary: Potosí mine has strong defensive geometry underground, but what kills you here is toxic air and chronic occupational health collapse.

global.name: Utqiagvik
global.summary: Extreme remoteness sharply reduces contact risk, but Arctic dependence makes long survival brittle.

global.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
global.summary: The Great Mosque of Djenné is visually imposing and culturally significant, but materially fragile for sustained defensive use. It may serve as a symbolic shelter point, yet structural vulnerability and limited isolation make it unsuitable as a serious long-term survival base.

global.name: Polar Observation Tower
global.summary: A high-visibility observation structure in an extreme polar environment. However, limited usable space, exposure, and system dependency make it a poor survival base.

global.name: Gaza Tunnel Network
global.summary: The Gaza tunnel network is formidable for concealment, but what kills you here is habitability collapse: air quality, sanitation, and medical limits degrade faster than tactical protection can compensate.

global.name: Hyundai Heavy Industries Shipyard
global.summary: Hyundai Shipyard has steel, machinery, and hard structures, but the footprint is too large and system-dependent to hold after logistics collapse. What kills you here is perimeter failure followed by cascading utility loss across an industrial maze.

global.name: Mombasa Port
global.summary: Mombasa Port provides throughput and maritime options, but as a permanent base it is dominated by exposure and contestability. The core trade-off is supply access versus impossible perimeter demand.

global.name: North Head Gun Emplacements
global.summary: North Head works as a hard defensive shell, but urban proximity and tiny sustainment depth make it a poor long-term base.

global.name: Tiruppur Textile Cluster
global.summary: Tiruppur’s textile cluster offers manufacturing utility but poor survival geometry; it is better treated as a salvage-and-fabrication zone than a residential base.

global.name: Murmansk Port
global.summary: Murmansk Port is useful for short-run cold-water logistics, but what kills you here is fuel-and-heating dependency: once industrial throughput drops, exposure and infrastructure decay outrun defense.

global.name: Wuhan Institute of Virology
global.summary: The Wuhan Institute of Virology offers a controlled campus with hardened buildings, but it sits inside a dense megacity ecosystem. What kills you here is sustained urban pressure that outlasts your supplies and manpower.

global.name: Kizhi Pogost
global.summary: Kizhi is remote and scenic, but what kills you here is infrastructure poverty: you run out of heat, medicine, and repair capacity before threats ever need to storm the site.

global.name: Rotterdam Port
global.summary: Rotterdam Port is an industrial jackpot for mobile operations; what kills you here is exposure from trying to hold an enormous contested perimeter.

global.name: Intramuros Manila
global.summary: Intramuros is a compact walled district that can delay pressure but not outlast a metropolis. It works for short defensive control through gates, walls, and predictable internal movement. You die when encirclement cuts supplies and crowd pressure overwhelms limited capacity.

global.name: Spinnaker Tower
global.summary: A tall urban landmark with excellent visibility but almost no practical survival value. It is exposed, space-limited, and surrounded by urban threat pressure, making it a poor base despite its height.

global.name: Cape Town Airport
global.summary: Cape Town Airport has impressive infrastructure but fails the base test because it concentrates movement, visibility, and conflict. The dominant trade-off is logistics access versus uncontrollable exposure.

global.name: Port of Murmansk
global.summary: Murmansk Port has strong maritime infrastructure and resource throughput, but high visibility and strategic exposure make it hard to secure in prolonged collapse.

global.name: Portsmouth Harbour
global.summary: Portsmouth Harbour gives mobility and maritime utility, but what kills you here is being continuously contested as a strategic coastal choke area.

global.name: Prudhoe Bay Oil Field
global.summary: Prudhoe Bay provides remote industrial assets, but it is not configured as a resilient civilian survival ecosystem.

global.name: Tokyo Airport
global.summary: Tokyo Airport gives mobility and infrastructure, but it concentrates traffic and threat. What kills you here is runway-scale exposure: you can move fast, but you cannot secure the footprint long enough to live there.

global.name: Cueva de las Manos
global.summary: Cueva de las Manos offers concealment and basic shelter, but what kills you here is resource starvation in a site that cannot scale into a living system.

global.name: General Santos Fish Port
global.summary: General Santos Fish Port is an industrial protein-conversion hub with limited defensive survivability. It works when fuel, labor, and cold-chain systems keep high-throughput processing alive. You die when utilities or security fail and spoilage outpaces usable output.

global.name: Phare du Créac'h
global.summary: Phare du Créac’h provides remote coastal isolation and observation value, but it is too small and brittle for extended habitation. What kills you here is capacity failure once stores run thin.

global.name: Uluru Surroundings
global.summary: Remote desert standoff lowers contact risk, but water and heat realities make it hard to sustain life.

global.name: Ghawar Oil Field Central Processing
global.summary: Ghawar processing nodes sit in relatively sparse terrain, but what kills you here is cascading industrial failure: hazardous systems and specialist dependencies turn quickly from asset to liability.

global.name: Abqaiq Oil Processing Facility
global.summary: Abqaiq has useful industrial assets, but what kills you here is strategic visibility: a famous energy node draws repeated attacks and requires fragile technical systems you cannot sustain locally.

global.name: Bunge Soy Processing Plant (Santos)
global.summary: Bunge Santos provides useful food-processing infrastructure, but it is an exposed industrial site that depends on fragile upstream and downstream networks.

global.name: Shanghai Port
global.summary: Shanghai Port has extraordinary logistics but zero survivable perimeter once order breaks down. What kills you here is endless contact pressure from people, fire, and conflict converging on critical cargo nodes.

global.name: Super Pit Gold Mine
global.summary: A giant pit gives visibility and machinery access, but it is an exposure trap with almost no resilient living envelope.

global.name: Port Arthur Refinery
global.summary: Port Arthur Refinery has immense industrial capacity, but its dominant failure mode is cascading industrial hazard: once maintenance and staffing quality drop, fire, toxic release, and perimeter chaos outpace any defensive benefit.

global.name: Phoenix Airfield (McMurdo)
global.summary: Phoenix Airfield is useful for movement and staging, but as a survival base it is a flat, exposed logistics point with almost no self-sustaining capacity.

global.name: Jebel Ali Port
global.summary: Jebel Ali carries huge logistics value, but what kills you here is strategic magnetism: ports attract organized competition, making stable governance and perimeter security unsustainable.

global.name: Helsinki Airport
global.summary: Helsinki Airport is a movement asset, not a sanctuary; what kills you here is continuous mass ingress that overwhelms perimeter control and resource security.

global.name: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse
global.summary: Excellent sightline tower in a hostile coastal strip; useful for watch duty, not for living.

global.name: Corwith Intermodal Yard
global.summary: Huge logistics surface with salvage value, but fundamentally indefensible as a survival base.

global.name: Mumbai Port
global.summary: Mumbai Port is a high-throughput maritime logistics hub, not a durable fortress. It works for rapid salvage and redistribution while port systems still function. You die when open coastal exposure and urban pressure overwhelm security and operational continuity.

global.name: Panama Canal Zone
global.summary: Panama Canal has infrastructure and throughput, but what kills you here is becoming a strategic flashpoint that cannot be isolated from conflict pressure.

global.name: Cape Byron Lighthouse
global.summary: Excellent lookout value does not translate into base value: this is an exposed observation point, not a survivable settlement.

global.name: Glacier Plateau
global.summary: Glacier terrain provides exceptional separation and approach control, but almost no independent life-support capacity.

global.name: Great Buddha Leshan
global.summary: Leshan’s landmark setting is symbolic, not survivable: it lacks perimeter control, shelter depth, and production capacity. What kills you here is exposure—too many approaches, too little infrastructure, no endurance.

global.name: São Paulo Airport
global.summary: São Paulo Airport is a logistics giant but a survival dead end: it offers short-lived salvage value and almost no defensible, low-pressure living profile.

global.name: Lighthouse Mahabalipuram
global.summary: Lighthouse Mahabalipuram is a coastal observation point, not a true survival base. It works for short surveillance and rendezvous because of elevation and clear sightlines. You die when external supplies stop, since the site has no durable food, water, or defensive depth.

global.name: Auckland Port
global.summary: Auckland Port is useful for fast salvage and maritime movement, but it collapses quickly as a static survival base.

global.name: Dubai Airport
global.summary: Dubai Airport has infrastructure abundance, but what kills you here is convergence pressure: every route, crowd, and claimant converges on the same open, high-value terrain.

global.name: Ostankino Tower
global.summary: Ostankino is a symbolic vertical landmark, not a survival base; what kills you here is siege and fire in a high-visibility trap with no resilient life-support depth.

global.name: Burj Khalifa
global.summary: Burj Khalifa looks defensible on paper, but what kills you here is infrastructure dependency cascade: elevators, pumping, cooling, and sanitation failures turn vertical shelter into a trapped population stack.

global.name: Charles de Gaulle Airport
global.summary: Charles de Gaulle Airport is a giant logistics surface but a catastrophic survival refuge. What kills you here is relentless exposure from scale, visibility, and traffic convergence.

global.name: Delhi Airport
global.summary: Delhi Airport is a massive transit complex suited only for short extraction operations. It works briefly because infrastructure density offers salvageable fuel, vehicles, and staging space. You die when perimeter control collapses under nonstop metropolitan inflow pressure.

global.name: Heathrow Airport
global.summary: Heathrow is resource-rich but fundamentally non-defensible at collapse scale; what kills you here is mass convergence and perimeter chaos within days.

global.name: Lighthouse Punta Del Este
global.summary: Punta lighthouse gives sightlines but almost no survivability; what kills you here is being fixed in a visible coastal choke point without supplies.

global.name: Schiphol Airport
global.summary: Schiphol has modern infrastructure but shares the same fatal profile as other mega-airports. What kills you here is nonstop exposure across open, high-traffic approach vectors.

global.name: CN Tower
global.summary: The CN Tower has surveillance value but fails as a survival base; its dominant failure mode is vertical entrapment: limited exits, no resource base, and dense urban surround turn height into a dead end.

global.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
global.summary: As a landmark chokepoint it has tactical relevance, but as a survival base it is functionally non-viable.

global.name: Tokyo Tower
global.summary: Tokyo Tower is an urban observation structure, not a survivable refuge. What kills you here is instant concentration risk: extreme visibility, no self-sufficiency, and no controllable defensive envelope.

global.name: Sydney Airport
global.summary: Sydney Airport is a movement asset only; as a survival base it is structurally non-viable.

global.name: Petronas Towers
global.summary: Petronas Towers are iconic urban high-rises with negligible collapse-survival utility. They work only as momentary observation or waypoint structures during movement. You die when dense-city convergence and utility failure remove access, water, and safe egress.

global.name: Qutub Minar
global.summary: Qutub Minar is an urban landmark that can serve as a waypoint but not a survivable base. It works only for brief navigation or coordination due to recognizability and height. You die from immediate urban pressure and zero on-site life-support capacity.

global.name: Christ the Redeemer
global.summary: Christ the Redeemer is a landmark, not a base; what kills you here is immediate exposure with no sustainment capacity.

global.name: Eiffel Tower
global.summary: The Eiffel Tower is a visibility trap, not a survival base. What kills you here is immediate exposure and zero self-sufficiency.

global.name: LAX Airport
global.summary: Massive infrastructure in the worst possible density context; viable only as a brief transit objective.

africa.name: Seychelles
africa.summary: Seychelles is one of the strongest African macro-base options because exceptional island isolation combines with a livable climate and realistic long-term habitation potential. The main constraint is coordination and resupply across dispersed islands once external systems weaken.

africa.name: Simien Mountains
africa.summary: The Simien Mountains are a naturally defensible high-altitude stronghold, where sheer cliffs, limited access routes, and extreme isolation significantly reduce external threat pressure. However, that same isolation severely limits long-term survivability, with constrained food production, harsh living conditions, and difficult resupply. Over time, the balance shifts from protection to restriction, making it better suited to short-term refuge than permanent settlement.

africa.name: Matmata Underground Dwellings
africa.summary: Matmata offers a strong concealment-defense package with naturally insulated subterranean housing and manageable access points. Its core trade-off is protected living space versus limited scale and external dependence for growth.

africa.name: Zanzibar Island
africa.summary: Zanzibar balances meaningful island separation with established settlement infrastructure, making it a credible medium-to-long-term refuge if governance and resource management remain coherent. Its challenge is that it is populated and close enough to mainland dynamics to face persistent pressure.

africa.name: Aït Benhaddou
africa.summary: Aït Benhaddou is a strong niche base: its fortified settlement form and relative isolation support controlled defense and lower immediate pressure. Its long-term ceiling is set by arid constraints, where limited water and food capacity become the decisive bottleneck.

africa.name: Fasil Ghebbi
africa.summary: Fasil Ghebbi is a fortified royal compound with thick masonry, layered courtyards, and strong internal control, giving it above-average defensive potential in an inland setting. It is more balanced than many heritage landmarks, but long-term survival still depends on building reliable food, water, and medical systems beyond the walls.

africa.name: Camp Lemonnier
africa.summary: Camp Lemonnier has exceptional military-grade defensive capability and organized base infrastructure, making it one of the strongest compounds in a direct security sense. But it is not highly independent: if fuel, water treatment, and logistics pipelines fail, performance drops fast.

africa.name: Table Mountain Plateau
africa.summary: Table Mountain Plateau is a highly defensible elevated position with steep cliffs, strong visibility, and usable space on top. However, its direct proximity to Cape Town, multiple access routes, and high visibility make it far less secure than more remote mountain strongholds. It is better suited to short-term defence and staging than long-term isolation.

africa.name: Elmina Castle
africa.summary: Elmina Castle is a heavily fortified coastal stronghold with thick walls, controlled internal spaces, and clear defensive advantages. However, its position within a populated coastal town and direct access from land and sea significantly reduce its long-term viability, making it better suited to temporary defence than sustained survival.

africa.name: Bonny Island LNG Terminal
africa.summary: Bonny LNG Terminal is a powerful industrial strongpoint with controlled space and hard infrastructure, but it is brittle under collapse conditions. Its usefulness depends on complex systems, skilled maintenance, and steady supply chains that are hard to replace locally.

africa.name: Kimberley Big Hole & Mining Complex
africa.summary: The Kimberley Big Hole offers strong terrain-based defensibility, but it is a dangerous bowl if exits, water access, or supply routes fail. It works as a hard-to-storm holdout early on, yet can quickly become a trap once core lifelines are cut.

africa.name: Waw an Namus Cave System
africa.summary: Waw an Namus is one of the hardest places to reach, which dramatically lowers threat pressure. The same isolation becomes the fatal weakness because survival systems are almost entirely import-dependent.

africa.name: Kolmanskop
africa.summary: Kolmanskop buys time through remoteness and clear sightlines, but it cannot feed or hydrate a group for long. The dominant trade-off is safety from people versus total dependence on imported water and food.

africa.name: UN Base in Juba (UNMISS HQ, South Sudan)
africa.summary: UNMISS Juba provides a protected compound that can absorb early shocks, but prolonged crisis drives mounting population pressure into and around the site. Over time, crowding and aid dependence overwhelm what the perimeter can realistically sustain.

africa.name: Cape Point Lighthouse
africa.summary: Cape Point Lighthouse has tactical lookout value and some geographic separation, but it lacks the carrying capacity and resource depth needed for sustained habitation. It works best as an observation and signaling outpost rather than a primary survival settlement.

africa.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
africa.summary: The Great Mosque of Djenné is visually imposing and culturally significant, but materially fragile for sustained defensive use. It may serve as a symbolic shelter point, yet structural vulnerability and limited isolation make it unsuitable as a serious long-term survival base.

africa.name: Mombasa Port
africa.summary: Mombasa Port provides throughput and maritime options, but as a permanent base it is dominated by exposure and contestability. The core trade-off is supply access versus impossible perimeter demand.

africa.name: Cape Town Airport
africa.summary: Cape Town Airport has impressive infrastructure but fails the base test because it concentrates movement, visibility, and conflict. The dominant trade-off is logistics access versus uncontrollable exposure.

east_asia.name: Jeju Island
east_asia.summary: Jeju is a strong island refuge with usable farmland, water access, and natural maritime separation from mainland spillover. What kills you here is maritime choke failure: if ports and fuel fail, an island-scale population can out-consume local capacity.

east_asia.name: Mount Huashan
east_asia.summary: Mount Huashan is an elite defensive perch with severe access control and strong natural isolation. The decisive trade-off is near-unmatched protection versus chronic logistical fragility.

east_asia.name: Great Wall Fortress Sections
east_asia.summary: Great Wall fortress sections provide strong engineered defense lines and terrain leverage, but they are fragmented assets rather than turnkey settlements. The dominant trade-off is excellent barrier control versus poor self-sustaining living capacity.

east_asia.name: Iwo Jima Underground Bunkers
east_asia.summary: Iwo Jima’s bunker network is exceptionally hard to assault and highly isolated, but it is austere and resource-poor. What kills you here is life-support collapse underground: water, ventilation, and medical limits outrun defensive advantages.

east_asia.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge Cliffs
east_asia.summary: Tiger Leaping Gorge offers extraordinary terrain defense and low approach density, but daily survival is constrained by space and supply movement. The central trade-off is tactical dominance versus unworkable sustainment at scale.

east_asia.name: Himeji Castle
east_asia.summary: Himeji Castle delivers high-quality fortress geometry and controlled internal defense, but its urban context limits long-term security. The key trade-off is superb structure versus low isolation.

east_asia.name: Okinawa
east_asia.summary: Okinawa offers meaningful island separation and workable living conditions, but dense infrastructure and strategic visibility increase contest pressure. What kills you here is competition over ports, fuel, and transport hubs that fractures island stability.

east_asia.name: Beijing Underground City
east_asia.summary: Beijing Underground City is hard to clear and hard to spot, but it is still a buried extension of a megacity. What kills you here is ventilation and water-system failure once surface utilities, filters, and spare parts stop flowing.

east_asia.name: Shirakawa-go
east_asia.summary: Shirakawa-go benefits from mountain remoteness and small-settlement cohesion, but severe winters and limited redundancy constrain endurance. What kills you here is winter logistics failure: heat, medicine, and mobility collapse before threats do.

east_asia.name: Shaxi Ancient Town
east_asia.summary: Shaxi is a remote town with manageable scale and decent local living potential, but it lacks hard defensive geometry. What kills you here is slow attrition from repeated incursions that drain manpower and stores.

east_asia.name: Ryongsong Residence Compound
east_asia.summary: Ryongsong Compound has strong perimeter control and internal zoning, but it remains a politically obvious fixed site in an urban state core. What kills you here is siege pressure once external support and movement options collapse.

east_asia.name: Foxconn Shenzhen Factory
east_asia.summary: The Shenzhen factory complex has unusual infrastructure depth and short-term resource potential, but it sits inside one of the world’s densest urban-industrial corridors. The dominant trade-off is internal capability versus catastrophic exposure.

east_asia.name: Hyundai Heavy Industries Shipyard
east_asia.summary: Hyundai Shipyard has steel, machinery, and hard structures, but the footprint is too large and system-dependent to hold after logistics collapse. What kills you here is perimeter failure followed by cascading utility loss across an industrial maze.

east_asia.name: Wuhan Institute of Virology
east_asia.summary: The Wuhan Institute of Virology offers a controlled campus with hardened buildings, but it sits inside a dense megacity ecosystem. What kills you here is sustained urban pressure that outlasts your supplies and manpower.

east_asia.name: Shanghai Port

east_asia.name: Great Buddha Leshan
east_asia.summary: Leshan’s landmark setting is symbolic, not survivable: it lacks perimeter control, shelter depth, and production capacity. What kills you here is exposure—too many approaches, too little infrastructure, no endurance.

east_asia.name: Tokyo Tower
east_asia.summary: Tokyo Tower is an urban observation structure, not a survivable refuge. What kills you here is instant concentration risk: extreme visibility, no self-sufficiency, and no controllable defensive envelope.

eastern_europe.name: Faroe Islands
eastern_europe.summary: Faroe is one of Europe's strongest isolation plays, but what kills you here is maritime bottleneck failure when storms, fuel limits, and fleet wear cut food and medical imports.

eastern_europe.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
eastern_europe.summary: Derinkuyu is an elite hide-and-hold refuge, but what kills you here is subterranean throughput collapse: ventilation, waste handling, and calorie flow fail before defenses do.

eastern_europe.name: Gotland
eastern_europe.summary: Gotland is a robust island option with workable infrastructure, but what kills you here is coastline overextension: too many access points for too few defenders over time.

eastern_europe.name: Malbork Castle
eastern_europe.summary: Malbork provides exceptional masonry defense and layered gates, but it sits in a reachable lowland region. What kills you here is siege attrition: repeated encirclement and supply disruption grind down even a strong fortress.

eastern_europe.name: Visby
eastern_europe.summary: Visby is a balanced walled island town, but what kills you here is population-and-water strain if too many survivors concentrate behind finite historic defenses.

eastern_europe.name: Predjama Castle
eastern_europe.summary: Predjama is a superb cliff fortress with choke-point control, but fortress geometry does not make food or medicine. What kills you here is siege starvation: you can deny entry for a long time and still lose to depletion.

eastern_europe.name: Suomenlinna Fortress
eastern_europe.summary: Suomenlinna has real island-fortress defensive logic, but it is tied to nearby urban waters and maritime supply. What kills you here is blockade-driven depletion when fuel, food, and treatment capacity cannot be replenished.

eastern_europe.name: Longyearbyen
eastern_europe.summary: A remote Arctic settlement with strong isolation, infrastructure, and controlled access. However, extreme climate and supply-chain reliance constrain long-term resilience.

eastern_europe.name: Norilsk
eastern_europe.summary: Norilsk is remote enough to avoid mass contact, but the environment itself is hostile to human endurance. What kills you here is infrastructure-coupled cold exposure: once heat, shelter integrity, or medical capability slip, mortality spikes fast.

eastern_europe.name: Olenya Air Base
eastern_europe.summary: Olenya can absorb early shock thanks to military-grade hardening and Arctic distance, but what kills you here is fuel-and-spares collapse in extreme cold once central logistics break.

eastern_europe.name: Ligatne Bunker
eastern_europe.summary: Ligatne's bunker geometry is excellent for sheltering, but what kills you here is air-power-water dependency: once life-support systems degrade, underground becomes a coffin.

eastern_europe.name: Gdańsk Shipyard
eastern_europe.summary: Gdańsk Shipyard is a high-value industrial toolkit, not a survivable sanctuary. What kills you here is perimeter overstretch: too much open infrastructure to guard, too many approach paths, too many competing groups.

eastern_europe.name: Chernobyl Exclusion Zone Facility
eastern_europe.summary: Chernobyl offers rare low-population isolation in Europe, but contamination and decaying infrastructure impose a slow-burn survival tax. What kills you here is cumulative exposure and medical degradation, not immediate assault.

eastern_europe.name: Murmansk Port
eastern_europe.summary: Murmansk Port is useful for short-run cold-water logistics, but what kills you here is fuel-and-heating dependency: once industrial throughput drops, exposure and infrastructure decay outrun defense.

eastern_europe.name: Helsinki Airport
eastern_europe.summary: Helsinki Airport is a movement asset, not a sanctuary; what kills you here is continuous mass ingress that overwhelms perimeter control and resource security.

eastern_europe.name: Ostankino Tower
eastern_europe.summary: Ostankino is a symbolic vertical landmark, not a survival base; what kills you here is siege and fire in a high-visibility trap with no resilient life-support depth.

middle_east.name: Socotra Island
middle_east.summary: Socotra gives outstanding separation from collapse corridors, but what kills you here is maritime supply fracture: once sea links fail, medicine, tools, and replacement goods run out faster than local systems can adapt.

middle_east.name: Krak des Chevaliers
middle_east.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a premier fortress for holding ground, but what kills you here is siege economics: ammunition, medicine, and calories run out long before the walls meaningfully fail.

middle_east.name: Cappadocia Highlands
middle_east.summary: Cappadocia’s broken terrain and concealment options make it a strong defensive refuge, but what kills you here is water-and-agriculture throughput: dispersed hideouts can outlast attacks, not prolonged scarcity.

middle_east.name: Siwa Oasis
middle_east.summary: Siwa Oasis is one of the more credible long-horizon refuges in the region, but what kills you here is water-system fragility: contamination, overdraw, or pump failure can collapse the settlement’s carrying capacity.

middle_east.name: Qeshm Island
middle_east.summary: Qeshm offers valuable island separation and room for mixed subsistence, but what kills you here is control dilution: the island is large enough that fragmented authority invites persistent infiltration and internal conflict.

middle_east.name: Masada
middle_east.summary: Masada is brutally hard to assault, but what kills you here is plateau logistics: water, heat management, and medical throughput collapse before attackers can force entry.

middle_east.name: Petra
middle_east.summary: Petra offers strong chokepoints and concealment in stone corridors, but what kills you here is water dependency: once stored supply and nearby sources are contested, defensive geometry cannot feed or hydrate a population.

middle_east.name: Al Udeid Air Base
middle_east.summary: Al Udeid provides one of the best ready-made defense envelopes in the region, but what kills you here is signature load: major airbase visibility attracts sustained external pressure and drains supplies.

middle_east.name: Wadi Musa
middle_east.summary: Wadi Musa is workable but fragile; what kills you here is corridor squeeze: limited approach routes become contested chokepoints that choke trade, movement, and medical evacuation.

middle_east.name: Ras Al Khair Desalination Plant
middle_east.summary: Ras Al Khair’s water output is uniquely valuable, but what kills you here is power-chain fragility: once energy input or specialist maintenance fails, the core survival advantage disappears fast.

middle_east.name: Lighthouse Hormuz
middle_east.summary: Hormuz lighthouse has useful separation and surveillance value, but what kills you here is capacity exhaustion: the site is too small and too harsh to sustain a community once short-term stores are depleted.

middle_east.name: Gaza Tunnel Network
middle_east.summary: The Gaza tunnel network is formidable for concealment, but what kills you here is habitability collapse: air quality, sanitation, and medical limits degrade faster than tactical protection can compensate.

middle_east.name: Ghawar Oil Field Central Processing

middle_east.summary: Jebel Ali carries huge logistics value, but what kills you here is strategic magnetism: ports attract organized competition, making stable governance and perimeter security unsustainable.

middle_east.name: Dubai Airport
middle_east.summary: Dubai Airport has infrastructure abundance, but what kills you here is convergence pressure: every route, crowd, and claimant converges on the same open, high-value terrain.

middle_east.name: Burj Khalifa
middle_east.summary: Burj Khalifa looks defensible on paper, but what kills you here is infrastructure dependency cascade: elevators, pumping, cooling, and sanitation failures turn vertical shelter into a trapped population stack.

north_america.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex
north_america.summary: Purpose-built hardened infrastructure makes this one of the most defensible options on the board.

north_america.name: Kodiak Island
north_america.summary: Kodiak is a high-isolation island with credible wild-resource potential, but its dominant failure mode is climate-logistics attrition: severe weather and seasonal bottlenecks steadily erode throughput, maintenance, and medical resilience.

north_america.name: Telluride
north_america.summary: Mountain terrain and manageable scale make Telluride a credible holdout if you prepare for winter logistics.

north_america.name: Titan Missile Museum (Silo 571-7)
north_america.summary: A tough underground shell with real protective value, but limited habitability without major adaptation.

north_america.name: Area 51
north_america.summary: Area 51 combines remoteness, controlled approaches, and hardened infrastructure, but its dominant failure mode is systems complexity debt: without specialized maintenance pipelines, high-tech capabilities decay into unusable overhead.

north_america.name: Alcatraz Island
north_america.summary: Alcatraz buys strong early security through water separation and choke-point access, but the decisive failure mode is supply starvation: once boat fuel, food inflow, and repair parts lapse, the island becomes a sealed deficit zone.

north_america.name: Mesa Verde
north_america.summary: Mesa Verde offers strong terrain defense, but what kills you here is carrying-capacity mismatch: protected positions can hold people, yet arable throughput and water logistics limit long-run population support.

north_america.name: Vancouver Island
north_america.summary: Vancouver Island is one of the most balanced large-island options, but its dominant failure mode is population-interface pressure: connected urban corridors and ferry chokepoints can overwhelm otherwise strong local resources.

north_america.name: Fort Jefferson
north_america.summary: Fort Jefferson is an exceptional sea-fortress with clear defensive geometry and extreme stand-off distance, but its dominant failure mode is water-energy fragility: if desalination and fuel chains degrade, habitability collapses quickly.

north_america.name: Guantanamo Bay
north_america.summary: Guantanamo offers strong perimeter control and organized facilities, yet the dominant failure mode is geopolitical encirclement: prolonged dependence on maritime logistics and contested sovereignty can choke continuity even before direct breach.

north_america.name: Table Rock Plateau
north_america.summary: Table Rock is a serviceable elevated fallback, but what kills you here is perimeter dilution: broad approach arcs and limited concealment stretch defenders until incidents become constant.

north_america.name: Hutchinson Salt Storage Caverns
north_america.summary: Hutchinson salt caverns provide excellent blast/weather protection and concealment, yet the single dominant failure mode is ventilation-power dependency: lose airflow and pumping reliability, and the underground advantage becomes a liability.

north_america.name: Utqiagvik
north_america.summary: Extreme remoteness sharply reduces contact risk, but Arctic dependence makes long survival brittle.

north_america.name: Port Arthur Refinery
north_america.summary: Port Arthur Refinery has immense industrial capacity, but its dominant failure mode is cascading industrial hazard: once maintenance and staffing quality drop, fire, toxic release, and perimeter chaos outpace any defensive benefit.

north_america.name: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse
north_america.summary: Excellent sightline tower in a hostile coastal strip; useful for watch duty, not for living.

north_america.name: Corwith Intermodal Yard
north_america.summary: Huge logistics surface with salvage value, but fundamentally indefensible as a survival base.

north_america.name: CN Tower
north_america.summary: The CN Tower has surveillance value but fails as a survival base; its dominant failure mode is vertical entrapment: limited exits, no resource base, and dense urban surround turn height into a dead end.

north_america.name: LAX Airport
north_america.summary: Massive infrastructure in the worst possible density context; viable only as a brief transit objective.

oceania.name: Tasmania
oceania.summary: Tasmania is one of the strongest balanced options: durable food-water-energy potential with enough separation to reduce pressure.

oceania.name: Fiji Islands
oceania.summary: Fiji balances isolation and livability better than most island options, but cyclone and maritime dependence cap reliability.

oceania.name: Coober Pedy Underground Settlement
oceania.summary: Coober Pedy is one of the few desert sites where underground habitation is already proven, but long-term success is limited by hard water and logistics ceilings.

oceania.name: RAAF Base Tindal
oceania.summary: High-grade military infrastructure gives strong initial control, but strategic visibility and supply dependence limit endurance.

oceania.name: Anna Creek Station
oceania.summary: Exceptional scale and remoteness support long-run survival potential, but the footprint is too vast to secure conventionally.

oceania.name: Maori Pa Fortifications
oceania.summary: Strong terrain-first fortifications can stop early incursions, but most pa sites fail once stocks and water run thin.

oceania.name: Pine Gap Facility
oceania.summary: Extreme remoteness and hardened controls are offset by acute system dependency and top-tier strategic exposure.

oceania.name: Blue Mountains Cliffs
oceania.summary: Excellent terrain defense and standoff distance, with sustainment limited by wildfire and infrastructure thinness.

oceania.name: Port Vila
oceania.summary: Port Vila offers real settlement infrastructure and island separation, but limited depth makes it fragile under prolonged disruption.

oceania.name: Fort Denison
oceania.summary: A compact fortified island position with controllable access but almost no independent sustainment depth.

oceania.name: North Head Gun Emplacements
oceania.summary: North Head works as a hard defensive shell, but urban proximity and tiny sustainment depth make it a poor long-term base.

oceania.name: Uluru Surroundings
oceania.summary: Remote desert standoff lowers contact risk, but water and heat realities make it hard to sustain life.

oceania.name: Super Pit Gold Mine
oceania.summary: A giant pit gives visibility and machinery access, but it is an exposure trap with almost no resilient living envelope.

oceania.name: Cape Byron Lighthouse
oceania.summary: Excellent lookout value does not translate into base value: this is an exposed observation point, not a survivable settlement.

oceania.name: Auckland Port
oceania.summary: Auckland Port is useful for fast salvage and maritime movement, but it collapses quickly as a static survival base.

oceania.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
oceania.summary: As a landmark chokepoint it has tactical relevance, but as a survival base it is functionally non-viable.

oceania.name: Sydney Airport
oceania.summary: Sydney Airport is a movement asset only; as a survival base it is structurally non-viable.

polar_extreme.name: Greenland
polar_extreme.summary: A vast Arctic island with extreme isolation, natural resources, and scattered settlements. However, harsh climate, huge scale, and infrastructure dependency make it difficult to control or sustain.

polar_extreme.name: Olavsvern Naval Base
polar_extreme.summary: A hardened underground naval base with strong concealment and protected infrastructure. However, confined systems, external supply needs, and limited scalability restrict long-term survival.

polar_extreme.name: Nagurskoye Air Base
polar_extreme.summary: A remote Arctic military airbase with controlled access and strong strategic positioning. However, extreme climate, visibility, and dependence on supply chains reduce independent survivability.

polar_extreme.name: McMurdo Station
polar_extreme.summary: A large Antarctic research station with infrastructure, shelter, and operational capacity. However, harsh conditions and dependence on supply chains limit true long-term independence.

polar_extreme.name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
polar_extreme.summary: An extremely isolated scientific station with controlled infrastructure and almost no external threat pressure. However, total dependence on life-support systems and resupply makes long-term independence impossible.

polar_extreme.name: Murmansk Icebreaker Port
polar_extreme.summary: A polar maritime hub with specialist icebreaker infrastructure and Arctic access. However, port exposure, supply dependency, and harsh operating conditions limit long-term security.

polar_extreme.name: Antarctic Peninsula
polar_extreme.summary: A remote polar region with natural isolation and access to coastal landing points. However, severe weather, limited infrastructure, and scarce sustainable resources make survival highly fragile.

polar_extreme.name: Camp Century Ice Tunnels
polar_extreme.summary: Camp Century is exceptionally hard to reach and hard to assault, but it fails as a settlement because the environment itself destroys long-term habitability.

polar_extreme.name: Crevasse Field Glacier
polar_extreme.summary: A fractured glacial terrain filled with deep crevasses, offering extreme isolation and natural barriers. However, unstable footing, concealed crevasse risk, and lack of resources make long-term survival nearly impossible.

polar_extreme.name: Antarctic Lighthouse
