polar_extreme.summary: A small polar outpost with visibility and isolation. However, exposure, limited shelter, and lack of resources make it unsuitable for long-term survival.

polar_extreme.name: Polar Observation Tower
polar_extreme.summary: A high-visibility observation structure in an extreme polar environment. However, limited usable space, exposure, and system dependency make it a poor survival base.

polar_extreme.name: Port of Murmansk
polar_extreme.summary: Murmansk Port has strong maritime infrastructure and resource throughput, but high visibility and strategic exposure make it hard to secure in prolonged collapse.

polar_extreme.name: Prudhoe Bay Oil Field
polar_extreme.summary: Prudhoe Bay provides remote industrial assets, but it is not configured as a resilient civilian survival ecosystem.

polar_extreme.name: Phoenix Airfield (McMurdo)
polar_extreme.summary: Phoenix Airfield is useful for movement and staging, but as a survival base it is a flat, exposed logistics point with almost no self-sustaining capacity.

polar_extreme.name: Glacier Plateau
polar_extreme.summary: Glacier terrain provides exceptional separation and approach control, but almost no independent life-support capacity.

south_america.name: Chiloé Island
south_america.summary: Chiloé is a strong all-round island base with workable agriculture and defensible approaches, but what kills you here is prolonged maritime cutoff during a hard winter.

south_america.name: Cusco Highlands Village
south_america.summary: Cusco highlands villages combine terrain defense with proven local subsistence systems, but what kills you here is cold-altitude medical decline in unacclimated groups.

south_america.name: Machu Picchu
south_america.summary: Machu Picchu offers excellent terrain defense and controlled approach lines, but limited productive capacity prevents large, permanent survival communities.

south_america.name: Galápagos Islands
south_america.summary: Galápagos has extreme isolation and low random threat traffic, but what kills you here is supply collapse once imported essentials stop.

south_america.name: Itaipu Dam
south_america.summary: Itaipu Dam has exceptional energy potential and water access, making it operationally powerful, but its scale and strategic value make defense extremely demanding.

south_america.name: San Felipe Fortress
south_america.summary: San Felipe combines historical fortification advantages with moderate operating feasibility, but limited local throughput caps long-term resilience.

south_america.name: Amazon Tall Tower Observatory
south_america.summary: ATTO offers deep-rainforest isolation and strong natural resource potential, but terrain, disease burden, and mobility constraints make control and continuity difficult.

south_america.name: Patagonian Village
south_america.summary: Patagonian villages benefit from remoteness and low traffic, but what kills you here is wind-cold exposure when fuel and shelter maintenance fall behind.

south_america.name: Tambopata Research Center
south_america.summary: Tambopata gives concealment and food potential in deep jungle, but what kills you here is untreated injury or infection far from reliable care.

south_america.name: Fort Copacabana
south_america.summary: Copacabana Fort is structurally robust and tactically defensible at the site level, but dense urban surroundings overwhelm long-term survivability.

south_america.name: La Rinconada
south_america.summary: La Rinconada gains protection from altitude and remoteness, but extreme living conditions and weak local systems limit survival duration.

south_america.name: Potosí Silver Mine (Cerro Rico)
south_america.summary: Potosí mine has strong defensive geometry underground, but what kills you here is toxic air and chronic occupational health collapse.

south_america.name: Cueva de las Manos
south_america.summary: Cueva de las Manos offers concealment and basic shelter, but what kills you here is resource starvation in a site that cannot scale into a living system.

south_america.name: Bunge Soy Processing Plant (Santos)
south_america.summary: Bunge Santos provides useful food-processing infrastructure, but it is an exposed industrial site that depends on fragile upstream and downstream networks.

south_america.name: Panama Canal Zone
south_america.summary: Panama Canal has infrastructure and throughput, but what kills you here is becoming a strategic flashpoint that cannot be isolated from conflict pressure.

south_america.name: São Paulo Airport
south_america.summary: São Paulo Airport is a logistics giant but a survival dead end: it offers short-lived salvage value and almost no defensible, low-pressure living profile.

south_america.name: Lighthouse Punta Del Este
south_america.summary: Punta lighthouse gives sightlines but almost no survivability; what kills you here is being fixed in a visible coastal choke point without supplies.

south_america.name: Christ the Redeemer
south_america.summary: Christ the Redeemer is a landmark, not a base; what kills you here is immediate exposure with no sustainment capacity.

south_asia.name: Andaman Islands
south_asia.summary: The Andamans are one of the strongest long-horizon options: maritime isolation and resource diversity create resilience if governance and inter-island logistics stay coherent.

south_asia.name: Mehrangarh Fort
south_asia.summary: Mehrangarh combines exceptional fortification geometry with workable internal scale, making it one of the stronger fortress options if surrounding pressure is actively managed.

south_asia.name: Hilltop Fort Rajasthan
south_asia.summary: A Rajasthan hill fort is a classic high-control stronghold with excellent wall geometry, but water and heat stress define whether it thrives or slowly fails.

south_asia.name: Sigiriya
south_asia.summary: Sigiriya offers rare rock-fortress defensibility and visibility, but constrained top-plateau capacity limits how long a group can live there without strong external support.

south_asia.name: Hanle Observatory
south_asia.summary: Hanle Observatory is an isolation-dominant survival option with low encounter pressure, but extreme altitude and remoteness impose severe physiological and logistics penalties.

south_asia.name: Kargil War Bunkers
south_asia.summary: Kargil War Bunkers are military-hardened high-altitude positions designed to resist assault. They work by combining strong fortification with terrain that channels approaches. You die when cold-weather fuel, medical, and resupply throughput collapses before defenses do.

south_asia.name: Tiger’s Nest Monastery
south_asia.summary: Tiger’s Nest is an extreme cliffside redoubt with elite access denial, but its tiny carrying capacity and severe logistics ceiling cap long-term survival.

south_asia.name: Pathankot Air Force Station
south_asia.summary: Pathankot AFS is a hardened operational compound with meaningful defensive structure, but its strategic visibility keeps pressure high and long-term autonomy uncertain.

south_asia.name: Kibber Village
south_asia.summary: Kibber is a high-altitude remote village that trades accessibility for security. It works through isolation, narrow approaches, and existing community housing for organized routines. You die when winter isolation, fuel gaps, or delayed medical care compound faster than recovery.

south_asia.name: Lakshadweep
south_asia.summary: Lakshadweep is a distributed island-chain refuge where sea separation reduces routine contact and gives strong early warning. It works when multiple islands coordinate boats, storage, and rationing as one system. You die when maritime links or freshwater discipline fail and each island is stranded alone.

south_asia.name: Ajanta Caves
south_asia.summary: Ajanta Caves are a hardened cave shelter system with strong choke-point defense. It works for short protected occupancy because rock-cut access geometry lowers breach risk. You die when confinement-driven sanitation and resource limits outrun defensive advantages.

south_asia.name: Kuttanad Village
south_asia.summary: Kuttanad is a food-producing lowland basin built around paddy and waterways. It works as a production engine when flood control, storage, and transport are tightly managed. You die when flooding and disease pressure break perimeter control and erase surplus.

south_asia.name: KRBL Rice Mill (Dhuri)
south_asia.summary: KRBL Dhuri has serious food-processing upside, but as a fixed base it is exposed, labor-dependent, and hard to secure against persistent pressure.

south_asia.name: Tiruppur Textile Cluster
south_asia.summary: Tiruppur’s textile cluster offers manufacturing utility but poor survival geometry; it is better treated as a salvage-and-fabrication zone than a residential base.

south_asia.name: Mumbai Port
south_asia.summary: Mumbai Port is a high-throughput maritime logistics hub, not a durable fortress. It works for rapid salvage and redistribution while port systems still function. You die when open coastal exposure and urban pressure overwhelm security and operational continuity.

south_asia.name: Lighthouse Mahabalipuram
south_asia.summary: Lighthouse Mahabalipuram is a coastal observation point, not a true survival base. It works for short surveillance and rendezvous because of elevation and clear sightlines. You die when external supplies stop, since the site has no durable food, water, or defensive depth.

south_asia.name: Delhi Airport
south_asia.summary: Delhi Airport is a massive transit complex suited only for short extraction operations. It works briefly because infrastructure density offers salvageable fuel, vehicles, and staging space. You die when perimeter control collapses under nonstop metropolitan inflow pressure.

south_asia.name: Qutub Minar
south_asia.summary: Qutub Minar is an urban landmark that can serve as a waypoint but not a survivable base. It works only for brief navigation or coordination due to recognizability and height. You die from immediate urban pressure and zero on-site life-support capacity.

southeast_asia.name: Palawan
southeast_asia.summary: Palawan is a large island system that balances isolation, defensibility, and resource diversity. It works when distributed settlements and logistics are coordinated at island-wide scale. You die when governance fractures and shipping disruption desynchronizes regional supply.

southeast_asia.name: Rice Terrace Highlands
southeast_asia.summary: Rice Terrace Highlands are elevated agrarian settlements with built-in food potential. They work by combining controllable approach routes with reliable staple production systems. You die when irrigation, labor coordination, or slope access fails during stress cycles.

southeast_asia.name: Banda Neira
southeast_asia.summary: A small island settlement with strong maritime separation, historic fortifications, and access to coastal resources. It works best as a low-profile island refuge, but limited scale and supply dependence cap long-term resilience.

southeast_asia.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
southeast_asia.summary: A purpose-built tunnel network with concealment, restricted access, and strong defensive history. It is highly effective for short-term evasion, but confinement, ventilation, and resource limits make permanent survival difficult.

southeast_asia.name: Ha Long Bay Cliffs
southeast_asia.summary: Ha Long Bay cliffs are a terrain-fragmented coastal redoubt of islands and vertical rock. It works by forcing movement through predictable maritime channels and narrow landing points. You die when weather or boat degradation cuts mobility and resupply between sectors.

southeast_asia.name: Hue Citadel
southeast_asia.summary: Hue Citadel is a fortified urban compound with layered walls and controlled gates. It works as a short-to-medium defensive enclave where geometry slows penetration. You die when siege pressure outlasts external food, fuel, and medical inflows.

southeast_asia.name: Komodo Island
southeast_asia.summary: Komodo is a highly isolated island refuge with strong separation from mainland pressure. It works by limiting approach routes and maintaining disciplined low-population maritime living. You die when freshwater constraints and sea-logistics disruption trigger cascading shortages.

southeast_asia.name: Vietnam Tunnel Systems
southeast_asia.summary: A broader tunnel-system concept with strong concealment and movement control across difficult terrain. It provides tactical advantage, but fragmented infrastructure and poor long-term livability keep it below true stronghold status.

southeast_asia.name: Danum Valley Field Centre
southeast_asia.summary: Danum Valley Field Centre is a remote jungle refuge with low-contact signature advantages. It works for small trained groups that can run strict field medicine and maintenance routines. You die when treatable illness, injury, or equipment failure outpaces evacuation and repair.

southeast_asia.name: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base
southeast_asia.summary: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base is a military command compound with strong tactical security. It works through hardened access control, organized response, and maritime support infrastructure. You die when prolonged contest burns fuel, parts, and readiness faster than resupply.

southeast_asia.name: Banlung
southeast_asia.summary: A remote inland town with surrounding terrain, forest cover, and regional resource access. It offers more livability than a pure wilderness refuge, but weak defensibility and difficult logistics limit its ceiling.

southeast_asia.name: Sime Darby Palm Oil Estate (Sabah)
southeast_asia.summary: Sime Darby Sabah is a large agro-industrial estate that can produce at regional scale. It works when core zones, mills, roads, and workforce discipline stay synchronized. You die when security overstretch and machinery dependence cause cascading output loss.

southeast_asia.name: Singapore Port
southeast_asia.summary: A globally significant port with exceptional logistics, maritime access, and infrastructure. Those strengths become liabilities in collapse, as exposure, density, and strategic importance make it almost impossible to hold.

southeast_asia.name: Bangkok Airport
southeast_asia.summary: A major transport hub with huge space, supplies, and infrastructure. It fails as a base because urban proximity, scale, and uncontrolled entry points make it impossible to secure.

southeast_asia.name: Phu Quoc Lighthouse
southeast_asia.summary: A coastal lighthouse with visibility, limited access, and some island separation. It offers short-term observation value, but exposure, lack of resources, and dependence on nearby settlement make it weak as a base.

southeast_asia.name: Intramuros Manila
southeast_asia.summary: Intramuros is a compact walled district that can delay pressure but not outlast a metropolis. It works for short defensive control through gates, walls, and predictable internal movement. You die when encirclement cuts supplies and crowd pressure overwhelms limited capacity.

southeast_asia.name: General Santos Fish Port
southeast_asia.summary: General Santos Fish Port is an industrial protein-conversion hub with limited defensive survivability. It works when fuel, labor, and cold-chain systems keep high-throughput processing alive. You die when utilities or security fail and spoilage outpaces usable output.

southeast_asia.name: Petronas Towers
southeast_asia.summary: Petronas Towers are iconic urban high-rises with negligible collapse-survival utility. They work only as momentary observation or waypoint structures during movement. You die when dense-city convergence and utility failure remove access, water, and safe egress.

uk_ireland.name: Isle of Eigg Village
uk_ireland.summary: Eigg is a rare island community with real off-grid credibility; what kills you here is a bad season that breaks food, fuel, and medical margins before security fails.

uk_ireland.name: Burlington Bunker
uk_ireland.summary: Burlington is exceptionally hard to breach in the opening phase; what kills you here is closed-system decay once consumables, maintenance, or governance slip.

uk_ireland.name: Lindisfarne
uk_ireland.summary: A tidal island with natural separation, limited access windows, and a defensible settlement pattern. It works well for a disciplined small group, but tide dependency and resource limits cap long-term resilience.

uk_ireland.name: Caerphilly Castle
uk_ireland.summary: A large moated castle with strong defensive design and layered barriers. It is one of the stronger historic fortifications, but modern exposure and limited self-sufficiency keep it from elite status.

uk_ireland.name: St Kilda
uk_ireland.summary: An extremely remote island archipelago with exceptional isolation and low external threat pressure. Its weakness is sustainment: weather, landing difficulty, and limited resources make survival fragile over time.

uk_ireland.name: Fort George
uk_ireland.summary: A purpose-built coastal military fort with strong walls, controlled access, and organised internal space. It has real defensive value, but exposure and reliance on external supplies limit long-term independence.

uk_ireland.name: HM Prison Dartmoor
uk_ireland.summary: A remote prison complex with secure walls, controlled movement, and strong internal containment. It offers a credible short-term defensive shell, but harsh exposure and limited self-sufficiency constrain long-term survival.

uk_ireland.name: Clovelly
uk_ireland.summary: A steep coastal village with constrained access routes, natural defensibility, and small-scale shelter. It is viable as a compact refuge, but limited expansion, coastal exposure, and supply dependence restrict long-term survival.

uk_ireland.name: Edinburgh Castle
uk_ireland.summary: A highly defensible urban castle on elevated rock, with strong visibility and controlled approaches. It is excellent as a symbolic redoubt, but urban exposure and limited sustainability reduce long-term value.

uk_ireland.name: Porton Down
uk_ireland.summary: A secure research facility with controlled access, specialist infrastructure, and perimeter discipline. It has defensive value, but technical dependency, contamination risk, and strategic visibility create serious long-term weakness.

uk_ireland.name: The Roaches
uk_ireland.summary: A rocky elevated ridge with natural defensibility, visibility, and difficult approaches. It works as a temporary fallback point, but exposure and lack of infrastructure make it unsuitable for long-term occupation.

uk_ireland.name: Amazon BHX4 Fulfilment Centre
uk_ireland.summary: A huge logistics warehouse with stored goods, space, and controlled internal areas. It gives a strong early advantage, but weak defensibility, dependence on systems, and surrounding access routes make it decay quickly.

uk_ireland.name: Port Talbot Steelworks
uk_ireland.summary: A major industrial site with infrastructure, materials, and repair potential. It is useful as a resource node, but pollution, exposure, and system dependency make it weak as a secure living base.

uk_ireland.name: Cheddar Gorge Caves
uk_ireland.summary: Cheddar Gorge caves are a solid tactical hide with useful terrain friction; what kills you here is chronic livability failure, not direct assault.

uk_ireland.name: Fastnet Lighthouse
uk_ireland.summary: A remote offshore lighthouse with extreme separation and strong visibility. It is nearly useless as a survival base because space, shelter, food, water, and evacuation options are all critically limited.

uk_ireland.name: Spinnaker Tower
uk_ireland.summary: A tall urban landmark with excellent visibility but almost no practical survival value. It is exposed, space-limited, and surrounded by urban threat pressure, making it a poor base despite its height.

uk_ireland.name: Portsmouth Harbour
uk_ireland.summary: Portsmouth Harbour gives mobility and maritime utility, but what kills you here is being continuously contested as a strategic coastal choke area.

uk_ireland.name: Heathrow Airport
uk_ireland.summary: Heathrow is resource-rich but fundamentally non-defensible at collapse scale; what kills you here is mass convergence and perimeter chaos within days.

western_europe.name: Mont Saint-Michel
western_europe.summary: Mont Saint-Michel is one of the hardest micro-sites to assault thanks to tidal separation; what kills you here is throughput limits in food, space, and medical response.

western_europe.name: Heligoland
western_europe.summary: Heligoland is one of the strongest isolation plays in Western Europe: remote, compact, and easier to monitor than mainland sites. What kills you here is maritime dependency when weather or fuel cuts the lifeline.

western_europe.name: Carcassonne
western_europe.summary: Carcassonne is a premier fortified shell with layered walls and command depth; what kills you here is sustainment fatigue behind intact defenses.

western_europe.name: 2e REP Barracks (Calvi)
western_europe.summary: 2e REP Calvi is a hard military compound with disciplined layout and perimeter control, but it sits on a populated island with finite local capacity. What kills you here is prolonged resupply failure after the initial defensive advantage burns off.

western_europe.name: Hallstatt
western_europe.summary: Hallstatt combines constrained access with strong local livability, making it one of the better balanced settlement options. What kills you here is chokepoint failure that traps residents against terrain.

western_europe.name: Île d’Yeu
western_europe.summary: Île d’Yeu is a balanced island refuge with useful separation and livable conditions, but it lacks deep strategic depth. What kills you here is slow resource depletion under prolonged isolation.

western_europe.name: Rocamadour
western_europe.summary: Rocamadour balances cliffside defense with workable rural linkage; what kills you here is exceeding carrying capacity and overloading water/sanitation systems.

western_europe.name: Maginot Line Bunkers
western_europe.summary: The Maginot bunkers are elite for hard protection but poor at independent endurance. What kills you here is subsystem failure underground: air, water, power, and sanitation.

western_europe.name: NATO Airbase Geilenkirchen
western_europe.summary: Geilenkirchen offers serious NATO-grade infrastructure and layered security, but it is embedded in dense mainland networks. What kills you here is constant contact pressure once perimeter staffing and logistics slip.

western_europe.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
western_europe.summary: Neuschwanstein offers strong terrain-assisted defense and visibility; what kills you here is logistics drag from a symbolic site that cannot feed itself.

western_europe.name: Ruhr Industrial Complex
western_europe.summary: The Ruhr offers broad industrial depth across many nodes; what kills you here is security sprawl that outgrows coordination capacity.

western_europe.name: Eguisheim
western_europe.summary: Eguisheim is a workable village-scale fallback with manageable density and access to surrounding land. What kills you here is perimeter dilution once pressure exceeds what a small settlement can police.

western_europe.name: Naours Underground City
western_europe.summary: Naours gives useful subterranean concealment and controlled entry, but it was never built as a full independent city. What kills you here is prolonged underground strain: air quality, hygiene, and supply depletion.

western_europe.name: Rotterdam Port
western_europe.summary: Rotterdam Port is an industrial jackpot for mobile operations; what kills you here is exposure from trying to hold an enormous contested perimeter.

western_europe.name: Phare du Créac'h
western_europe.summary: Phare du Créac’h provides remote coastal isolation and observation value, but it is too small and brittle for extended habitation. What kills you here is capacity failure once stores run thin.

western_europe.name: Charles de Gaulle Airport
western_europe.summary: Charles de Gaulle Airport is a giant logistics surface but a catastrophic survival refuge. What kills you here is relentless exposure from scale, visibility, and traffic convergence.

western_europe.name: Schiphol Airport
western_europe.summary: Schiphol has modern infrastructure but shares the same fatal profile as other mega-airports. What kills you here is nonstop exposure across open, high-traffic approach vectors.

western_europe.name: Eiffel Tower
western_europe.summary: The Eiffel Tower is a visibility trap, not a survival base. What kills you here is immediate exposure and zero self-sufficiency.

elevated_stronghold.name: Machu Picchu
elevated_stronghold.summary: Machu Picchu offers excellent terrain defense and controlled approach lines, but limited productive capacity prevents large, permanent survival communities.

elevated_stronghold.name: Simien Mountains
elevated_stronghold.summary: The Simien Mountains are a naturally defensible high-altitude stronghold, where sheer cliffs, limited access routes, and extreme isolation significantly reduce external threat pressure. However, that same isolation severely limits long-term survivability, with constrained food production, harsh living conditions, and difficult resupply. Over time, the balance shifts from protection to restriction, making it better suited to short-term refuge than permanent settlement.

elevated_stronghold.name: Hilltop Fort Rajasthan
elevated_stronghold.summary: A Rajasthan hill fort is a classic high-control stronghold with excellent wall geometry, but water and heat stress define whether it thrives or slowly fails.

elevated_stronghold.name: Rice Terrace Highlands
elevated_stronghold.summary: Rice Terrace Highlands are elevated agrarian settlements with built-in food potential. They work by combining controllable approach routes with reliable staple production systems. You die when irrigation, labor coordination, or slope access fails during stress cycles.

elevated_stronghold.name: Sigiriya
elevated_stronghold.summary: Sigiriya offers rare rock-fortress defensibility and visibility, but constrained top-plateau capacity limits how long a group can live there without strong external support.

elevated_stronghold.name: Cappadocia Highlands
elevated_stronghold.summary: Cappadocia’s broken terrain and concealment options make it a strong defensive refuge, but what kills you here is water-and-agriculture throughput: dispersed hideouts can outlast attacks, not prolonged scarcity.

elevated_stronghold.name: Mount Huashan
elevated_stronghold.summary: Mount Huashan is an elite defensive perch with severe access control and strong natural isolation. The decisive trade-off is near-unmatched protection versus chronic logistical fragility.

elevated_stronghold.name: Predjama Castle
elevated_stronghold.summary: Predjama is a superb cliff fortress with choke-point control, but fortress geometry does not make food or medicine. What kills you here is siege starvation: you can deny entry for a long time and still lose to depletion.

elevated_stronghold.name: Rocamadour
elevated_stronghold.summary: Rocamadour balances cliffside defense with workable rural linkage; what kills you here is exceeding carrying capacity and overloading water/sanitation systems.

elevated_stronghold.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge Cliffs
elevated_stronghold.summary: Tiger Leaping Gorge offers extraordinary terrain defense and low approach density, but daily survival is constrained by space and supply movement. The central trade-off is tactical dominance versus unworkable sustainment at scale.

elevated_stronghold.name: Tiger’s Nest Monastery
elevated_stronghold.summary: Tiger’s Nest is an extreme cliffside redoubt with elite access denial, but its tiny carrying capacity and severe logistics ceiling cap long-term survival.

elevated_stronghold.name: Mesa Verde
elevated_stronghold.summary: Mesa Verde offers strong terrain defense, but what kills you here is carrying-capacity mismatch: protected positions can hold people, yet arable throughput and water logistics limit long-run population support.

elevated_stronghold.name: Ha Long Bay Cliffs
elevated_stronghold.summary: Ha Long Bay cliffs are a terrain-fragmented coastal redoubt of islands and vertical rock. It works by forcing movement through predictable maritime channels and narrow landing points. You die when weather or boat degradation cuts mobility and resupply between sectors.

elevated_stronghold.name: Edinburgh Castle
elevated_stronghold.summary: A highly defensible urban castle on elevated rock, with strong visibility and controlled approaches. It is excellent as a symbolic redoubt, but urban exposure and limited sustainability reduce long-term value.

elevated_stronghold.name: Table Mountain Plateau
elevated_stronghold.summary: Table Mountain Plateau is a highly defensible elevated position with steep cliffs, strong visibility, and usable space on top. However, its direct proximity to Cape Town, multiple access routes, and high visibility make it far less secure than more remote mountain strongholds. It is better suited to short-term defence and staging than long-term isolation.

elevated_stronghold.name: Petra
elevated_stronghold.summary: Petra offers strong chokepoints and concealment in stone corridors, but what kills you here is water dependency: once stored supply and nearby sources are contested, defensive geometry cannot feed or hydrate a population.

elevated_stronghold.name: Table Rock Plateau
elevated_stronghold.summary: Table Rock is a serviceable elevated fallback, but what kills you here is perimeter dilution: broad approach arcs and limited concealment stretch defenders until incidents become constant.

elevated_stronghold.name: Blue Mountains Cliffs
elevated_stronghold.summary: Excellent terrain defense and standoff distance, with sustainment limited by wildfire and infrastructure thinness.

elevated_stronghold.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
elevated_stronghold.summary: Neuschwanstein offers strong terrain-assisted defense and visibility; what kills you here is logistics drag from a symbolic site that cannot feed itself.

elevated_stronghold.name: The Roaches
elevated_stronghold.summary: A rocky elevated ridge with natural defensibility, visibility, and difficult approaches. It works as a temporary fallback point, but exposure and lack of infrastructure make it unsuitable for long-term occupation.

elevated_stronghold.name: La Rinconada
elevated_stronghold.summary: La Rinconada gains protection from altitude and remoteness, but extreme living conditions and weak local systems limit survival duration.

elevated_stronghold.name: Uluru Surroundings
elevated_stronghold.summary: Remote desert standoff lowers contact risk, but water and heat realities make it hard to sustain life.

elevated_stronghold.name: Glacier Plateau
elevated_stronghold.summary: Glacier terrain provides exceptional separation and approach control, but almost no independent life-support capacity.

fortified_structure.name: Mont Saint-Michel
fortified_structure.summary: Mont Saint-Michel is one of the hardest micro-sites to assault thanks to tidal separation; what kills you here is throughput limits in food, space, and medical response.

fortified_structure.name: Mehrangarh Fort
fortified_structure.summary: Mehrangarh combines exceptional fortification geometry with workable internal scale, making it one of the stronger fortress options if surrounding pressure is actively managed.

fortified_structure.name: Carcassonne
fortified_structure.summary: Carcassonne is a premier fortified shell with layered walls and command depth; what kills you here is sustainment fatigue behind intact defenses.

fortified_structure.name: Krak des Chevaliers
fortified_structure.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a premier fortress for holding ground, but what kills you here is siege economics: ammunition, medicine, and calories run out long before the walls meaningfully fail.

fortified_structure.name: Great Wall Fortress Sections
fortified_structure.summary: Great Wall fortress sections provide strong engineered defense lines and terrain leverage, but they are fragmented assets rather than turnkey settlements. The dominant trade-off is excellent barrier control versus poor self-sustaining living capacity.

fortified_structure.name: Malbork Castle
fortified_structure.summary: Malbork provides exceptional masonry defense and layered gates, but it sits in a reachable lowland region. What kills you here is siege attrition: repeated encirclement and supply disruption grind down even a strong fortress.

fortified_structure.name: Fasil Ghebbi
fortified_structure.summary: Fasil Ghebbi is a fortified royal compound with thick masonry, layered courtyards, and strong internal control, giving it above-average defensive potential in an inland setting. It is more balanced than many heritage landmarks, but long-term survival still depends on building reliable food, water, and medical systems beyond the walls.

fortified_structure.name: Alcatraz Island
fortified_structure.summary: Alcatraz buys strong early security through water separation and choke-point access, but the decisive failure mode is supply starvation: once boat fuel, food inflow, and repair parts lapse, the island becomes a sealed deficit zone.

fortified_structure.name: Caerphilly Castle
fortified_structure.summary: A large moated castle with strong defensive design and layered barriers. It is one of the stronger historic fortifications, but modern exposure and limited self-sufficiency keep it from elite status.

fortified_structure.name: Himeji Castle
fortified_structure.summary: Himeji Castle delivers high-quality fortress geometry and controlled internal defense, but its urban context limits long-term security. The key trade-off is superb structure versus low isolation.

fortified_structure.name: Masada
fortified_structure.summary: Masada is brutally hard to assault, but what kills you here is plateau logistics: water, heat management, and medical throughput collapse before attackers can force entry.

fortified_structure.name: Fort George
fortified_structure.summary: A purpose-built coastal military fort with strong walls, controlled access, and organised internal space. It has real defensive value, but exposure and reliance on external supplies limit long-term independence.

fortified_structure.name: Fort Jefferson
fortified_structure.summary: Fort Jefferson is an exceptional sea-fortress with clear defensive geometry and extreme stand-off distance, but its dominant failure mode is water-energy fragility: if desalination and fuel chains degrade, habitability collapses quickly.

fortified_structure.name: Hue Citadel
fortified_structure.summary: Hue Citadel is a fortified urban compound with layered walls and controlled gates. It works as a short-to-medium defensive enclave where geometry slows penetration. You die when siege pressure outlasts external food, fuel, and medical inflows.

fortified_structure.name: Maori Pa Fortifications
fortified_structure.summary: Strong terrain-first fortifications can stop early incursions, but most pa sites fail once stocks and water run thin.

fortified_structure.name: Suomenlinna Fortress
fortified_structure.summary: Suomenlinna has real island-fortress defensive logic, but it is tied to nearby urban waters and maritime supply. What kills you here is blockade-driven depletion when fuel, food, and treatment capacity cannot be replenished.

fortified_structure.name: McMurdo Station
fortified_structure.summary: A large Antarctic research station with infrastructure, shelter, and operational capacity. However, harsh conditions and dependence on supply chains limit true long-term independence.

fortified_structure.name: San Felipe Fortress
fortified_structure.summary: San Felipe combines historical fortification advantages with moderate operating feasibility, but limited local throughput caps long-term resilience.

fortified_structure.name: Elmina Castle
fortified_structure.summary: Elmina Castle is a heavily fortified coastal stronghold with thick walls, controlled internal spaces, and clear defensive advantages. However, its position within a populated coastal town and direct access from land and sea significantly reduce its long-term viability, making it better suited to temporary defence than sustained survival.

fortified_structure.name: Fort Copacabana
fortified_structure.summary: Copacabana Fort is structurally robust and tactically defensible at the site level, but dense urban surroundings overwhelm long-term survivability.

fortified_structure.name: Fort Denison
fortified_structure.summary: A compact fortified island position with controllable access but almost no independent sustainment depth.

fortified_structure.name: Intramuros Manila
fortified_structure.summary: Intramuros is a compact walled district that can delay pressure but not outlast a metropolis. It works for short defensive control through gates, walls, and predictable internal movement. You die when encirclement cuts supplies and crowd pressure overwhelms limited capacity.

industrial_site.name: Anna Creek Station
industrial_site.summary: Exceptional scale and remoteness support long-run survival potential, but the footprint is too vast to secure conventionally.

industrial_site.name: Itaipu Dam
industrial_site.summary: Itaipu Dam has exceptional energy potential and water access, making it operationally powerful, but its scale and strategic value make defense extremely demanding.

industrial_site.name: Murmansk Icebreaker Port
industrial_site.summary: A polar maritime hub with specialist icebreaker infrastructure and Arctic access. However, port exposure, supply dependency, and harsh operating conditions limit long-term security.

industrial_site.name: Bonny Island LNG Terminal
industrial_site.summary: Bonny LNG Terminal is a powerful industrial strongpoint with controlled space and hard infrastructure, but it is brittle under collapse conditions. Its usefulness depends on complex systems, skilled maintenance, and steady supply chains that are hard to replace locally.

industrial_site.name: Sime Darby Palm Oil Estate (Sabah)
industrial_site.summary: Sime Darby Sabah is a large agro-industrial estate that can produce at regional scale. It works when core zones, mills, roads, and workforce discipline stay synchronized. You die when security overstretch and machinery dependence cause cascading output loss.

industrial_site.name: Kimberley Big Hole & Mining Complex
industrial_site.summary: The Kimberley Big Hole offers strong terrain-based defensibility, but it is a dangerous bowl if exits, water access, or supply routes fail. It works as a hard-to-storm holdout early on, yet can quickly become a trap once core lifelines are cut.

industrial_site.name: Hutchinson Salt Storage Caverns
industrial_site.summary: Hutchinson salt caverns provide excellent blast/weather protection and concealment, yet the single dominant failure mode is ventilation-power dependency: lose airflow and pumping reliability, and the underground advantage becomes a liability.

industrial_site.name: Norilsk
industrial_site.summary: Norilsk is remote enough to avoid mass contact, but the environment itself is hostile to human endurance. What kills you here is infrastructure-coupled cold exposure: once heat, shelter integrity, or medical capability slip, mortality spikes fast.

industrial_site.name: Ras Al Khair Desalination Plant
industrial_site.summary: Ras Al Khair’s water output is uniquely valuable, but what kills you here is power-chain fragility: once energy input or specialist maintenance fails, the core survival advantage disappears fast.

industrial_site.name: Amazon BHX4 Fulfilment Centre
industrial_site.summary: A huge logistics warehouse with stored goods, space, and controlled internal areas. It gives a strong early advantage, but weak defensibility, dependence on systems, and surrounding access routes make it decay quickly.

industrial_site.name: Port Talbot Steelworks
industrial_site.summary: A major industrial site with infrastructure, materials, and repair potential. It is useful as a resource node, but pollution, exposure, and system dependency make it weak as a secure living base.

industrial_site.name: Foxconn Shenzhen Factory
industrial_site.summary: The Shenzhen factory complex has unusual infrastructure depth and short-term resource potential, but it sits inside one of the world’s densest urban-industrial corridors. The dominant trade-off is internal capability versus catastrophic exposure.

industrial_site.name: Gdańsk Shipyard
industrial_site.summary: Gdańsk Shipyard is a high-value industrial toolkit, not a survivable sanctuary. What kills you here is perimeter overstretch: too much open infrastructure to guard, too many approach paths, too many competing groups.

industrial_site.name: KRBL Rice Mill (Dhuri)
industrial_site.summary: KRBL Dhuri has serious food-processing upside, but as a fixed base it is exposed, labor-dependent, and hard to secure against persistent pressure.

industrial_site.name: Ruhr Industrial Complex
industrial_site.summary: The Ruhr offers broad industrial depth across many nodes; what kills you here is security sprawl that outgrows coordination capacity.

industrial_site.name: Hyundai Heavy Industries Shipyard
industrial_site.summary: Hyundai Shipyard has steel, machinery, and hard structures, but the footprint is too large and system-dependent to hold after logistics collapse. What kills you here is perimeter failure followed by cascading utility loss across an industrial maze.

industrial_site.name: Tiruppur Textile Cluster
industrial_site.summary: Tiruppur’s textile cluster offers manufacturing utility but poor survival geometry; it is better treated as a salvage-and-fabrication zone than a residential base.

industrial_site.name: Rotterdam Port
industrial_site.summary: Rotterdam Port is an industrial jackpot for mobile operations; what kills you here is exposure from trying to hold an enormous contested perimeter.

industrial_site.name: Prudhoe Bay Oil Field
industrial_site.summary: Prudhoe Bay provides remote industrial assets, but it is not configured as a resilient civilian survival ecosystem.

industrial_site.name: General Santos Fish Port
industrial_site.summary: General Santos Fish Port is an industrial protein-conversion hub with limited defensive survivability. It works when fuel, labor, and cold-chain systems keep high-throughput processing alive. You die when utilities or security fail and spoilage outpaces usable output.

industrial_site.name: Abqaiq Oil Processing Facility
industrial_site.summary: Abqaiq has useful industrial assets, but what kills you here is strategic visibility: a famous energy node draws repeated attacks and requires fragile technical systems you cannot sustain locally.

industrial_site.name: Bunge Soy Processing Plant (Santos)
industrial_site.summary: Bunge Santos provides useful food-processing infrastructure, but it is an exposed industrial site that depends on fragile upstream and downstream networks.

industrial_site.name: Super Pit Gold Mine
industrial_site.summary: A giant pit gives visibility and machinery access, but it is an exposure trap with almost no resilient living envelope.

industrial_site.name: Port Arthur Refinery
industrial_site.summary: Port Arthur Refinery has immense industrial capacity, but its dominant failure mode is cascading industrial hazard: once maintenance and staffing quality drop, fire, toxic release, and perimeter chaos outpace any defensive benefit.

institutional_compound.name: Hanle Observatory
institutional_compound.summary: Hanle Observatory is an isolation-dominant survival option with low encounter pressure, but extreme altitude and remoteness impose severe physiological and logistics penalties.

institutional_compound.name: 2e REP Barracks (Calvi)
institutional_compound.summary: 2e REP Calvi is a hard military compound with disciplined layout and perimeter control, but it sits on a populated island with finite local capacity. What kills you here is prolonged resupply failure after the initial defensive advantage burns off.

institutional_compound.name: Area 51
institutional_compound.summary: Area 51 combines remoteness, controlled approaches, and hardened infrastructure, but its dominant failure mode is systems complexity debt: without specialized maintenance pipelines, high-tech capabilities decay into unusable overhead.

institutional_compound.name: RAAF Base Tindal
institutional_compound.summary: High-grade military infrastructure gives strong initial control, but strategic visibility and supply dependence limit endurance.

institutional_compound.name: Nagurskoye Air Base
institutional_compound.summary: A remote Arctic military airbase with controlled access and strong strategic positioning. However, extreme climate, visibility, and dependence on supply chains reduce independent survivability.

institutional_compound.name: Camp Lemonnier
institutional_compound.summary: Camp Lemonnier has exceptional military-grade defensive capability and organized base infrastructure, making it one of the strongest compounds in a direct security sense. But it is not highly independent: if fuel, water treatment, and logistics pipelines fail, performance drops fast.

institutional_compound.name: HM Prison Dartmoor
institutional_compound.summary: A remote prison complex with secure walls, controlled movement, and strong internal containment. It offers a credible short-term defensive shell, but harsh exposure and limited self-sufficiency constrain long-term survival.

institutional_compound.name: Pathankot Air Force Station
institutional_compound.summary: Pathankot AFS is a hardened operational compound with meaningful defensive structure, but its strategic visibility keeps pressure high and long-term autonomy uncertain.

institutional_compound.name: Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station
institutional_compound.summary: An extremely isolated scientific station with controlled infrastructure and almost no external threat pressure. However, total dependence on life-support systems and resupply makes long-term independence impossible.

institutional_compound.name: Danum Valley Field Centre
institutional_compound.summary: Danum Valley Field Centre is a remote jungle refuge with low-contact signature advantages. It works for small trained groups that can run strict field medicine and maintenance routines. You die when treatable illness, injury, or equipment failure outpaces evacuation and repair.

institutional_compound.name: Pine Gap Facility
institutional_compound.summary: Extreme remoteness and hardened controls are offset by acute system dependency and top-tier strategic exposure.

institutional_compound.name: Al Udeid Air Base
institutional_compound.summary: Al Udeid provides one of the best ready-made defense envelopes in the region, but what kills you here is signature load: major airbase visibility attracts sustained external pressure and drains supplies.

institutional_compound.name: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base
institutional_compound.summary: Kota Kinabalu Naval Base is a military command compound with strong tactical security. It works through hardened access control, organized response, and maritime support infrastructure. You die when prolonged contest burns fuel, parts, and readiness faster than resupply.

institutional_compound.name: Amazon Tall Tower Observatory
institutional_compound.summary: ATTO offers deep-rainforest isolation and strong natural resource potential, but terrain, disease burden, and mobility constraints make control and continuity difficult.

institutional_compound.name: Guantanamo Bay
institutional_compound.summary: Guantanamo offers strong perimeter control and organized facilities, yet the dominant failure mode is geopolitical encirclement: prolonged dependence on maritime logistics and contested sovereignty can choke continuity even before direct breach.

institutional_compound.name: Porton Down
institutional_compound.summary: A secure research facility with controlled access, specialist infrastructure, and perimeter discipline. It has defensive value, but technical dependency, contamination risk, and strategic visibility create serious long-term weakness.

institutional_compound.name: NATO Airbase Geilenkirchen
institutional_compound.summary: Geilenkirchen offers serious NATO-grade infrastructure and layered security, but it is embedded in dense mainland networks. What kills you here is constant contact pressure once perimeter staffing and logistics slip.

institutional_compound.name: Tambopata Research Center
institutional_compound.summary: Tambopata gives concealment and food potential in deep jungle, but what kills you here is untreated injury or infection far from reliable care.

institutional_compound.name: Olenya Air Base
institutional_compound.summary: Olenya can absorb early shock thanks to military-grade hardening and Arctic distance, but what kills you here is fuel-and-spares collapse in extreme cold once central logistics break.

institutional_compound.name: Ryongsong Residence Compound
institutional_compound.summary: Ryongsong Compound has strong perimeter control and internal zoning, but it remains a politically obvious fixed site in an urban state core. What kills you here is siege pressure once external support and movement options collapse.

institutional_compound.name: UN Base in Juba (UNMISS HQ, South Sudan)
institutional_compound.summary: UNMISS Juba provides a protected compound that can absorb early shocks, but prolonged crisis drives mounting population pressure into and around the site. Over time, crowding and aid dependence overwhelm what the perimeter can realistically sustain.

institutional_compound.name: Chernobyl Exclusion Zone Facility
institutional_compound.summary: Chernobyl offers rare low-population isolation in Europe, but contamination and decaying infrastructure impose a slow-burn survival tax. What kills you here is cumulative exposure and medical degradation, not immediate assault.

institutional_compound.name: Wuhan Institute of Virology
institutional_compound.summary: The Wuhan Institute of Virology offers a controlled campus with hardened buildings, but it sits inside a dense megacity ecosystem. What kills you here is sustained urban pressure that outlasts your supplies and manpower.

institutional_compound.name: Ghawar Oil Field Central Processing
institutional_compound.summary: Ghawar processing nodes sit in relatively sparse terrain, but what kills you here is cascading industrial failure: hazardous systems and specialist dependencies turn quickly from asset to liability.

isolated_landmass.name: Andaman Islands
isolated_landmass.summary: The Andamans are one of the strongest long-horizon options: maritime isolation and resource diversity create resilience if governance and inter-island logistics stay coherent.

isolated_landmass.name: Tasmania
isolated_landmass.summary: Tasmania is one of the strongest balanced options: durable food-water-energy potential with enough separation to reduce pressure.

isolated_landmass.name: Chiloé Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Chiloé is a strong all-round island base with workable agriculture and defensible approaches, but what kills you here is prolonged maritime cutoff during a hard winter.

isolated_landmass.name: Heligoland
isolated_landmass.summary: Heligoland is one of the strongest isolation plays in Western Europe: remote, compact, and easier to monitor than mainland sites. What kills you here is maritime dependency when weather or fuel cuts the lifeline.

isolated_landmass.name: Seychelles
isolated_landmass.summary: Seychelles is one of the strongest African macro-base options because exceptional island isolation combines with a livable climate and realistic long-term habitation potential. The main constraint is coordination and resupply across dispersed islands once external systems weaken.

isolated_landmass.name: Faroe Islands
isolated_landmass.summary: Faroe is one of Europe's strongest isolation plays, but what kills you here is maritime bottleneck failure when storms, fuel limits, and fleet wear cut food and medical imports.

isolated_landmass.name: Socotra Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Socotra gives outstanding separation from collapse corridors, but what kills you here is maritime supply fracture: once sea links fail, medicine, tools, and replacement goods run out faster than local systems can adapt.

isolated_landmass.name: Fiji Islands
isolated_landmass.summary: Fiji balances isolation and livability better than most island options, but cyclone and maritime dependence cap reliability.

isolated_landmass.name: Palawan
isolated_landmass.summary: Palawan is a large island system that balances isolation, defensibility, and resource diversity. It works when distributed settlements and logistics are coordinated at island-wide scale. You die when governance fractures and shipping disruption desynchronizes regional supply.

isolated_landmass.name: Kodiak Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Kodiak is a high-isolation island with credible wild-resource potential, but its dominant failure mode is climate-logistics attrition: severe weather and seasonal bottlenecks steadily erode throughput, maintenance, and medical resilience.

isolated_landmass.name: Zanzibar Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Zanzibar balances meaningful island separation with established settlement infrastructure, making it a credible medium-to-long-term refuge if governance and resource management remain coherent. Its challenge is that it is populated and close enough to mainland dynamics to face persistent pressure.

isolated_landmass.name: Gotland
isolated_landmass.summary: Gotland is a robust island option with workable infrastructure, but what kills you here is coastline overextension: too many access points for too few defenders over time.

isolated_landmass.name: Jeju Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Jeju is a strong island refuge with usable farmland, water access, and natural maritime separation from mainland spillover. What kills you here is maritime choke failure: if ports and fuel fail, an island-scale population can out-consume local capacity.

isolated_landmass.name: Galápagos Islands
isolated_landmass.summary: Galápagos has extreme isolation and low random threat traffic, but what kills you here is supply collapse once imported essentials stop.

isolated_landmass.name: Île d’Yeu
isolated_landmass.summary: Île d’Yeu is a balanced island refuge with useful separation and livable conditions, but it lacks deep strategic depth. What kills you here is slow resource depletion under prolonged isolation.

isolated_landmass.name: Lindisfarne
isolated_landmass.summary: A tidal island with natural separation, limited access windows, and a defensible settlement pattern. It works well for a disciplined small group, but tide dependency and resource limits cap long-term resilience.

isolated_landmass.name: Qeshm Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Qeshm offers valuable island separation and room for mixed subsistence, but what kills you here is control dilution: the island is large enough that fragmented authority invites persistent infiltration and internal conflict.

isolated_landmass.name: Greenland
isolated_landmass.summary: A vast Arctic island with extreme isolation, natural resources, and scattered settlements. However, harsh climate, huge scale, and infrastructure dependency make it difficult to control or sustain.

isolated_landmass.name: St Kilda
isolated_landmass.summary: An extremely remote island archipelago with exceptional isolation and low external threat pressure. Its weakness is sustainment: weather, landing difficulty, and limited resources make survival fragile over time.

isolated_landmass.name: Vancouver Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Vancouver Island is one of the most balanced large-island options, but its dominant failure mode is population-interface pressure: connected urban corridors and ferry chokepoints can overwhelm otherwise strong local resources.

isolated_landmass.name: Komodo Island
isolated_landmass.summary: Komodo is a highly isolated island refuge with strong separation from mainland pressure. It works by limiting approach routes and maintaining disciplined low-population maritime living. You die when freshwater constraints and sea-logistics disruption trigger cascading shortages.

isolated_landmass.name: Lakshadweep
isolated_landmass.summary: Lakshadweep is a distributed island-chain refuge where sea separation reduces routine contact and gives strong early warning. It works when multiple islands coordinate boats, storage, and rationing as one system. You die when maritime links or freshwater discipline fail and each island is stranded alone.

isolated_landmass.name: Antarctic Peninsula
isolated_landmass.summary: A remote polar region with natural isolation and access to coastal landing points. However, severe weather, limited infrastructure, and scarce sustainable resources make survival highly fragile.

isolated_landmass.name: Okinawa
isolated_landmass.summary: Okinawa offers meaningful island separation and workable living conditions, but dense infrastructure and strategic visibility increase contest pressure. What kills you here is competition over ports, fuel, and transport hubs that fractures island stability.

landmark_structure.name: Lighthouse Hormuz
landmark_structure.summary: Hormuz lighthouse has useful separation and surveillance value, but what kills you here is capacity exhaustion: the site is too small and too harsh to sustain a community once short-term stores are depleted.

landmark_structure.name: Phu Quoc Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: A coastal lighthouse with visibility, limited access, and some island separation. It offers short-term observation value, but exposure, lack of resources, and dependence on nearby settlement make it weak as a base.

landmark_structure.name: Cape Point Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: Cape Point Lighthouse has tactical lookout value and some geographic separation, but it lacks the carrying capacity and resource depth needed for sustained habitation. It works best as an observation and signaling outpost rather than a primary survival settlement.

landmark_structure.name: Fastnet Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: A remote offshore lighthouse with extreme separation and strong visibility. It is nearly useless as a survival base because space, shelter, food, water, and evacuation options are all critically limited.

landmark_structure.name: Antarctic Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: A small polar outpost with visibility and isolation. However, exposure, limited shelter, and lack of resources make it unsuitable for long-term survival.

landmark_structure.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
landmark_structure.summary: The Great Mosque of Djenné is visually imposing and culturally significant, but materially fragile for sustained defensive use. It may serve as a symbolic shelter point, yet structural vulnerability and limited isolation make it unsuitable as a serious long-term survival base.

landmark_structure.name: Polar Observation Tower
landmark_structure.summary: A high-visibility observation structure in an extreme polar environment. However, limited usable space, exposure, and system dependency make it a poor survival base.

landmark_structure.name: Kizhi Pogost
landmark_structure.summary: Kizhi is remote and scenic, but what kills you here is infrastructure poverty: you run out of heat, medicine, and repair capacity before threats ever need to storm the site.

landmark_structure.name: Spinnaker Tower
landmark_structure.summary: A tall urban landmark with excellent visibility but almost no practical survival value. It is exposed, space-limited, and surrounded by urban threat pressure, making it a poor base despite its height.

landmark_structure.name: Phare du Créac'h
landmark_structure.summary: Phare du Créac’h provides remote coastal isolation and observation value, but it is too small and brittle for extended habitation. What kills you here is capacity failure once stores run thin.

landmark_structure.name: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: Excellent sightline tower in a hostile coastal strip; useful for watch duty, not for living.

landmark_structure.name: Cape Byron Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: Excellent lookout value does not translate into base value: this is an exposed observation point, not a survivable settlement.

landmark_structure.name: Great Buddha Leshan
landmark_structure.summary: Leshan’s landmark setting is symbolic, not survivable: it lacks perimeter control, shelter depth, and production capacity. What kills you here is exposure—too many approaches, too little infrastructure, no endurance.

landmark_structure.name: Lighthouse Mahabalipuram
landmark_structure.summary: Lighthouse Mahabalipuram is a coastal observation point, not a true survival base. It works for short surveillance and rendezvous because of elevation and clear sightlines. You die when external supplies stop, since the site has no durable food, water, or defensive depth.

landmark_structure.name: Ostankino Tower
landmark_structure.summary: Ostankino is a symbolic vertical landmark, not a survival base; what kills you here is siege and fire in a high-visibility trap with no resilient life-support depth.

landmark_structure.name: Burj Khalifa
landmark_structure.summary: Burj Khalifa looks defensible on paper, but what kills you here is infrastructure dependency cascade: elevators, pumping, cooling, and sanitation failures turn vertical shelter into a trapped population stack.

landmark_structure.name: Lighthouse Punta Del Este
landmark_structure.summary: Punta lighthouse gives sightlines but almost no survivability; what kills you here is being fixed in a visible coastal choke point without supplies.

landmark_structure.name: CN Tower
landmark_structure.summary: The CN Tower has surveillance value but fails as a survival base; its dominant failure mode is vertical entrapment: limited exits, no resource base, and dense urban surround turn height into a dead end.

landmark_structure.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
landmark_structure.summary: As a landmark chokepoint it has tactical relevance, but as a survival base it is functionally non-viable.

landmark_structure.name: Tokyo Tower
landmark_structure.summary: Tokyo Tower is an urban observation structure, not a survivable refuge. What kills you here is instant concentration risk: extreme visibility, no self-sufficiency, and no controllable defensive envelope.

landmark_structure.name: Petronas Towers
landmark_structure.summary: Petronas Towers are iconic urban high-rises with negligible collapse-survival utility. They work only as momentary observation or waypoint structures during movement. You die when dense-city convergence and utility failure remove access, water, and safe egress.

landmark_structure.name: Qutub Minar
landmark_structure.summary: Qutub Minar is an urban landmark that can serve as a waypoint but not a survivable base. It works only for brief navigation or coordination due to recognizability and height. You die from immediate urban pressure and zero on-site life-support capacity.

landmark_structure.name: Christ the Redeemer
landmark_structure.summary: Christ the Redeemer is a landmark, not a base; what kills you here is immediate exposure with no sustainment capacity.

landmark_structure.name: Eiffel Tower
landmark_structure.summary: The Eiffel Tower is a visibility trap, not a survival base. What kills you here is immediate exposure and zero self-sufficiency.

polar_extreme.name: Crevasse Field Glacier
polar_extreme.summary: A fractured glacial terrain filled with deep crevasses, offering extreme isolation and natural barriers. However, unstable footing, concealed crevasse risk, and lack of resources make long-term survival nearly impossible.

remote_settlement.name: Isle of Eigg Village
remote_settlement.summary: Eigg is a rare island community with real off-grid credibility; what kills you here is a bad season that breaks food, fuel, and medical margins before security fails.

remote_settlement.name: Cusco Highlands Village
remote_settlement.summary: Cusco highlands villages combine terrain defense with proven local subsistence systems, but what kills you here is cold-altitude medical decline in unacclimated groups.

remote_settlement.name: Coober Pedy Underground Settlement
remote_settlement.summary: Coober Pedy is one of the few desert sites where underground habitation is already proven, but long-term success is limited by hard water and logistics ceilings.

remote_settlement.name: Siwa Oasis
remote_settlement.summary: Siwa Oasis is one of the more credible long-horizon refuges in the region, but what kills you here is water-system fragility: contamination, overdraw, or pump failure can collapse the settlement’s carrying capacity.

remote_settlement.name: Aït Benhaddou
remote_settlement.summary: Aït Benhaddou is a strong niche base: its fortified settlement form and relative isolation support controlled defense and lower immediate pressure. Its long-term ceiling is set by arid constraints, where limited water and food capacity become the decisive bottleneck.

remote_settlement.name: Hallstatt
remote_settlement.summary: Hallstatt combines constrained access with strong local livability, making it one of the better balanced settlement options. What kills you here is chokepoint failure that traps residents against terrain.

remote_settlement.name: Telluride
remote_settlement.summary: Mountain terrain and manageable scale make Telluride a credible holdout if you prepare for winter logistics.

remote_settlement.name: Visby
remote_settlement.summary: Visby is a balanced walled island town, but what kills you here is population-and-water strain if too many survivors concentrate behind finite historic defenses.

remote_settlement.name: Banda Neira
remote_settlement.summary: A small island settlement with strong maritime separation, historic fortifications, and access to coastal resources. It works best as a low-profile island refuge, but limited scale and supply dependence cap long-term resilience.

remote_settlement.name: Clovelly
remote_settlement.summary: A steep coastal village with constrained access routes, natural defensibility, and small-scale shelter. It is viable as a compact refuge, but limited expansion, coastal exposure, and supply dependence restrict long-term survival.

remote_settlement.name: Kibber Village
remote_settlement.summary: Kibber is a high-altitude remote village that trades accessibility for security. It works through isolation, narrow approaches, and existing community housing for organized routines. You die when winter isolation, fuel gaps, or delayed medical care compound faster than recovery.

remote_settlement.name: Longyearbyen
remote_settlement.summary: A remote Arctic settlement with strong isolation, infrastructure, and controlled access. However, extreme climate and supply-chain reliance constrain long-term resilience.

remote_settlement.name: Banlung
remote_settlement.summary: A remote inland town with surrounding terrain, forest cover, and regional resource access. It offers more livability than a pure wilderness refuge, but weak defensibility and difficult logistics limit its ceiling.

remote_settlement.name: Patagonian Village
remote_settlement.summary: Patagonian villages benefit from remoteness and low traffic, but what kills you here is wind-cold exposure when fuel and shelter maintenance fall behind.

remote_settlement.name: Shirakawa-go
remote_settlement.summary: Shirakawa-go benefits from mountain remoteness and small-settlement cohesion, but severe winters and limited redundancy constrain endurance. What kills you here is winter logistics failure: heat, medicine, and mobility collapse before threats do.

remote_settlement.name: Port Vila
remote_settlement.summary: Port Vila offers real settlement infrastructure and island separation, but limited depth makes it fragile under prolonged disruption.

remote_settlement.name: Wadi Musa
remote_settlement.summary: Wadi Musa is workable but fragile; what kills you here is corridor squeeze: limited approach routes become contested chokepoints that choke trade, movement, and medical evacuation.

remote_settlement.name: Shaxi Ancient Town
remote_settlement.summary: Shaxi is a remote town with manageable scale and decent local living potential, but it lacks hard defensive geometry. What kills you here is slow attrition from repeated incursions that drain manpower and stores.

remote_settlement.name: Kuttanad Village
remote_settlement.summary: Kuttanad is a food-producing lowland basin built around paddy and waterways. It works as a production engine when flood control, storage, and transport are tightly managed. You die when flooding and disease pressure break perimeter control and erase surplus.

remote_settlement.name: Kolmanskop
remote_settlement.summary: Kolmanskop buys time through remoteness and clear sightlines, but it cannot feed or hydrate a group for long. The dominant trade-off is safety from people versus total dependence on imported water and food.

remote_settlement.name: Eguisheim
remote_settlement.summary: Eguisheim is a workable village-scale fallback with manageable density and access to surrounding land. What kills you here is perimeter dilution once pressure exceeds what a small settlement can police.

remote_settlement.name: Utqiagvik
remote_settlement.summary: Extreme remoteness sharply reduces contact risk, but Arctic dependence makes long survival brittle.

subterranean.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex
subterranean.summary: Purpose-built hardened infrastructure makes this one of the most defensible options on the board.

subterranean.name: Matmata Underground Dwellings
subterranean.summary: Matmata offers a strong concealment-defense package with naturally insulated subterranean housing and manageable access points. Its core trade-off is protected living space versus limited scale and external dependence for growth.

subterranean.name: Burlington Bunker
subterranean.summary: Burlington is exceptionally hard to breach in the opening phase; what kills you here is closed-system decay once consumables, maintenance, or governance slip.

subterranean.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
subterranean.summary: Derinkuyu is an elite hide-and-hold refuge, but what kills you here is subterranean throughput collapse: ventilation, waste handling, and calorie flow fail before defenses do.

subterranean.name: Kargil War Bunkers
subterranean.summary: Kargil War Bunkers are military-hardened high-altitude positions designed to resist assault. They work by combining strong fortification with terrain that channels approaches. You die when cold-weather fuel, medical, and resupply throughput collapses before defenses do.

subterranean.name: Iwo Jima Underground Bunkers
subterranean.summary: Iwo Jima’s bunker network is exceptionally hard to assault and highly isolated, but it is austere and resource-poor. What kills you here is life-support collapse underground: water, ventilation, and medical limits outrun defensive advantages.

subterranean.name: Titan Missile Museum (Silo 571-7)
subterranean.summary: A tough underground shell with real protective value, but limited habitability without major adaptation.

subterranean.name: Olavsvern Naval Base
subterranean.summary: A hardened underground naval base with strong concealment and protected infrastructure. However, confined systems, external supply needs, and limited scalability restrict long-term survival.

subterranean.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
subterranean.summary: A purpose-built tunnel network with concealment, restricted access, and strong defensive history. It is highly effective for short-term evasion, but confinement, ventilation, and resource limits make permanent survival difficult.

subterranean.name: Vietnam Tunnel Systems
subterranean.summary: A broader tunnel-system concept with strong concealment and movement control across difficult terrain. It provides tactical advantage, but fragmented infrastructure and poor long-term livability keep it below true stronghold status.

subterranean.name: Beijing Underground City
subterranean.summary: Beijing Underground City is hard to clear and hard to spot, but it is still a buried extension of a megacity. What kills you here is ventilation and water-system failure once surface utilities, filters, and spare parts stop flowing.

subterranean.name: Maginot Line Bunkers
subterranean.summary: The Maginot bunkers are elite for hard protection but poor at independent endurance. What kills you here is subsystem failure underground: air, water, power, and sanitation.

subterranean.name: Camp Century Ice Tunnels
subterranean.summary: Camp Century is exceptionally hard to reach and hard to assault, but it fails as a settlement because the environment itself destroys long-term habitability.

subterranean.name: Waw an Namus Cave System
subterranean.summary: Waw an Namus is one of the hardest places to reach, which dramatically lowers threat pressure. The same isolation becomes the fatal weakness because survival systems are almost entirely import-dependent.

subterranean.name: Ajanta Caves
subterranean.summary: Ajanta Caves are a hardened cave shelter system with strong choke-point defense. It works for short protected occupancy because rock-cut access geometry lowers breach risk. You die when confinement-driven sanitation and resource limits outrun defensive advantages.

subterranean.name: Ligatne Bunker
subterranean.summary: Ligatne's bunker geometry is excellent for sheltering, but what kills you here is air-power-water dependency: once life-support systems degrade, underground becomes a coffin.

subterranean.name: Cheddar Gorge Caves
subterranean.summary: Cheddar Gorge caves are a solid tactical hide with useful terrain friction; what kills you here is chronic livability failure, not direct assault.

subterranean.name: Naours Underground City
subterranean.summary: Naours gives useful subterranean concealment and controlled entry, but it was never built as a full independent city. What kills you here is prolonged underground strain: air quality, hygiene, and supply depletion.

subterranean.name: Potosí Silver Mine (Cerro Rico)
subterranean.summary: Potosí mine has strong defensive geometry underground, but what kills you here is toxic air and chronic occupational health collapse.

subterranean.name: Gaza Tunnel Network
subterranean.summary: The Gaza tunnel network is formidable for concealment, but what kills you here is habitability collapse: air quality, sanitation, and medical limits degrade faster than tactical protection can compensate.

subterranean.name: North Head Gun Emplacements
subterranean.summary: North Head works as a hard defensive shell, but urban proximity and tiny sustainment depth make it a poor long-term base.

subterranean.name: Cueva de las Manos
subterranean.summary: Cueva de las Manos offers concealment and basic shelter, but what kills you here is resource starvation in a site that cannot scale into a living system.

transit_hub.name: Singapore Port
transit_hub.summary: A globally significant port with exceptional logistics, maritime access, and infrastructure. Those strengths become liabilities in collapse, as exposure, density, and strategic importance make it almost impossible to hold.

transit_hub.name: Bangkok Airport
transit_hub.summary: A major transport hub with huge space, supplies, and infrastructure. It fails as a base because urban proximity, scale, and uncontrolled entry points make it impossible to secure.

transit_hub.name: Mombasa Port
transit_hub.summary: Mombasa Port provides throughput and maritime options, but as a permanent base it is dominated by exposure and contestability. The core trade-off is supply access versus impossible perimeter demand.

transit_hub.name: Murmansk Port
transit_hub.summary: Murmansk Port is useful for short-run cold-water logistics, but what kills you here is fuel-and-heating dependency: once industrial throughput drops, exposure and infrastructure decay outrun defense.

transit_hub.name: Cape Town Airport
transit_hub.summary: Cape Town Airport has impressive infrastructure but fails the base test because it concentrates movement, visibility, and conflict. The dominant trade-off is logistics access versus uncontrollable exposure.

transit_hub.name: Port of Murmansk
transit_hub.summary: Murmansk Port has strong maritime infrastructure and resource throughput, but high visibility and strategic exposure make it hard to secure in prolonged collapse.

transit_hub.name: Portsmouth Harbour
transit_hub.summary: Portsmouth Harbour gives mobility and maritime utility, but what kills you here is being continuously contested as a strategic coastal choke area.

transit_hub.name: Tokyo Airport
transit_hub.summary: Tokyo Airport gives mobility and infrastructure, but it concentrates traffic and threat. What kills you here is runway-scale exposure: you can move fast, but you cannot secure the footprint long enough to live there.

transit_hub.name: Shanghai Port
transit_hub.summary: Shanghai Port has extraordinary logistics but zero survivable perimeter once order breaks down. What kills you here is endless contact pressure from people, fire, and conflict converging on critical cargo nodes.

transit_hub.name: Phoenix Airfield (McMurdo)
transit_hub.summary: Phoenix Airfield is useful for movement and staging, but as a survival base it is a flat, exposed logistics point with almost no self-sustaining capacity.

transit_hub.name: Jebel Ali Port
transit_hub.summary: Jebel Ali carries huge logistics value, but what kills you here is strategic magnetism: ports attract organized competition, making stable governance and perimeter security unsustainable.

transit_hub.name: Helsinki Airport
transit_hub.summary: Helsinki Airport is a movement asset, not a sanctuary; what kills you here is continuous mass ingress that overwhelms perimeter control and resource security.

transit_hub.name: Corwith Intermodal Yard
transit_hub.summary: Huge logistics surface with salvage value, but fundamentally indefensible as a survival base.

transit_hub.name: Mumbai Port
transit_hub.summary: Mumbai Port is a high-throughput maritime logistics hub, not a durable fortress. It works for rapid salvage and redistribution while port systems still function. You die when open coastal exposure and urban pressure overwhelm security and operational continuity.

transit_hub.name: Panama Canal Zone
transit_hub.summary: Panama Canal has infrastructure and throughput, but what kills you here is becoming a strategic flashpoint that cannot be isolated from conflict pressure.

transit_hub.name: São Paulo Airport
transit_hub.summary: São Paulo Airport is a logistics giant but a survival dead end: it offers short-lived salvage value and almost no defensible, low-pressure living profile.

transit_hub.name: Auckland Port
transit_hub.summary: Auckland Port is useful for fast salvage and maritime movement, but it collapses quickly as a static survival base.

transit_hub.name: Dubai Airport
transit_hub.summary: Dubai Airport has infrastructure abundance, but what kills you here is convergence pressure: every route, crowd, and claimant converges on the same open, high-value terrain.

transit_hub.name: Charles de Gaulle Airport
transit_hub.summary: Charles de Gaulle Airport is a giant logistics surface but a catastrophic survival refuge. What kills you here is relentless exposure from scale, visibility, and traffic convergence.

transit_hub.name: Delhi Airport
