transit_hub.summary: Delhi Airport is a massive transit complex suited only for short extraction operations. It works briefly because infrastructure density offers salvageable fuel, vehicles, and staging space. You die when perimeter control collapses under nonstop metropolitan inflow pressure.

transit_hub.name: Heathrow Airport
transit_hub.summary: Heathrow is resource-rich but fundamentally non-defensible at collapse scale; what kills you here is mass convergence and perimeter chaos within days.

transit_hub.name: Schiphol Airport
transit_hub.summary: Schiphol has modern infrastructure but shares the same fatal profile as other mega-airports. What kills you here is nonstop exposure across open, high-traffic approach vectors.

transit_hub.name: Sydney Airport
transit_hub.summary: Sydney Airport is a movement asset only; as a survival base it is structurally non-viable.

transit_hub.name: LAX Airport
transit_hub.summary: Massive infrastructure in the worst possible density context; viable only as a brief transit objective.

africa.name: Seychelles
africa.summary: Seychelles is one of the strongest African macro-base options because exceptional island isolation combines with a livable climate and realistic long-term habitation potential. The main constraint is coordination and resupply across dispersed islands once external systems weaken.

africa.name: Simien Mountains
africa.summary: The Simien Mountains are a naturally defensible high-altitude stronghold, where sheer cliffs, limited access routes, and extreme isolation significantly reduce external threat pressure. However, that same isolation severely limits long-term survivability, with constrained food production, harsh living conditions, and difficult resupply. Over time, the balance shifts from protection to restriction, making it better suited to short-term refuge than permanent settlement.

africa.name: Matmata Underground Dwellings
africa.summary: Matmata offers a strong concealment-defense package with naturally insulated subterranean housing and manageable access points. Its core trade-off is protected living space versus limited scale and external dependence for growth.

east_asia.name: Jeju Island
east_asia.summary: Jeju is a strong island refuge with usable farmland, water access, and natural maritime separation from mainland spillover. What kills you here is maritime choke failure: if ports and fuel fail, an island-scale population can out-consume local capacity.

east_asia.name: Mount Huashan
east_asia.summary: Mount Huashan is an elite defensive perch with severe access control and strong natural isolation. The decisive trade-off is near-unmatched protection versus chronic logistical fragility.

east_asia.name: Great Wall Fortress Sections
east_asia.summary: Great Wall fortress sections provide strong engineered defense lines and terrain leverage, but they are fragmented assets rather than turnkey settlements. The dominant trade-off is excellent barrier control versus poor self-sustaining living capacity.

eastern_europe.name: Faroe Islands
eastern_europe.summary: Faroe is one of Europe's strongest isolation plays, but what kills you here is maritime bottleneck failure when storms, fuel limits, and fleet wear cut food and medical imports.

eastern_europe.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
eastern_europe.summary: Derinkuyu is an elite hide-and-hold refuge, but what kills you here is subterranean throughput collapse: ventilation, waste handling, and calorie flow fail before defenses do.

eastern_europe.name: Gotland
eastern_europe.summary: Gotland is a robust island option with workable infrastructure, but what kills you here is coastline overextension: too many access points for too few defenders over time.

middle_east.name: Socotra Island
middle_east.summary: Socotra gives outstanding separation from collapse corridors, but what kills you here is maritime supply fracture: once sea links fail, medicine, tools, and replacement goods run out faster than local systems can adapt.

middle_east.name: Krak des Chevaliers
middle_east.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a premier fortress for holding ground, but what kills you here is siege economics: ammunition, medicine, and calories run out long before the walls meaningfully fail.

middle_east.name: Cappadocia Highlands
middle_east.summary: Cappadocia’s broken terrain and concealment options make it a strong defensive refuge, but what kills you here is water-and-agriculture throughput: dispersed hideouts can outlast attacks, not prolonged scarcity.

north_america.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex
north_america.summary: Purpose-built hardened infrastructure makes this one of the most defensible options on the board.

north_america.name: Kodiak Island
north_america.summary: Kodiak is a high-isolation island with credible wild-resource potential, but its dominant failure mode is climate-logistics attrition: severe weather and seasonal bottlenecks steadily erode throughput, maintenance, and medical resilience.

north_america.name: Telluride
north_america.summary: Mountain terrain and manageable scale make Telluride a credible holdout if you prepare for winter logistics.

oceania.name: Tasmania
oceania.summary: Tasmania is one of the strongest balanced options: durable food-water-energy potential with enough separation to reduce pressure.

oceania.name: Fiji Islands
oceania.summary: Fiji balances isolation and livability better than most island options, but cyclone and maritime dependence cap reliability.

oceania.name: Coober Pedy Underground Settlement
oceania.summary: Coober Pedy is one of the few desert sites where underground habitation is already proven, but long-term success is limited by hard water and logistics ceilings.

polar_extreme.name: Greenland
polar_extreme.summary: A vast Arctic island with extreme isolation, natural resources, and scattered settlements. However, harsh climate, huge scale, and infrastructure dependency make it difficult to control or sustain.

polar_extreme.name: Olavsvern Naval Base
polar_extreme.summary: A hardened underground naval base with strong concealment and protected infrastructure. However, confined systems, external supply needs, and limited scalability restrict long-term survival.

polar_extreme.name: Nagurskoye Air Base
polar_extreme.summary: A remote Arctic military airbase with controlled access and strong strategic positioning. However, extreme climate, visibility, and dependence on supply chains reduce independent survivability.

south_america.name: Chiloé Island
south_america.summary: Chiloé is a strong all-round island base with workable agriculture and defensible approaches, but what kills you here is prolonged maritime cutoff during a hard winter.

south_america.name: Cusco Highlands Village
south_america.summary: Cusco highlands villages combine terrain defense with proven local subsistence systems, but what kills you here is cold-altitude medical decline in unacclimated groups.

south_america.name: Machu Picchu
south_america.summary: Machu Picchu offers excellent terrain defense and controlled approach lines, but limited productive capacity prevents large, permanent survival communities.

south_asia.name: Andaman Islands
south_asia.summary: The Andamans are one of the strongest long-horizon options: maritime isolation and resource diversity create resilience if governance and inter-island logistics stay coherent.

south_asia.name: Mehrangarh Fort
south_asia.summary: Mehrangarh combines exceptional fortification geometry with workable internal scale, making it one of the stronger fortress options if surrounding pressure is actively managed.

south_asia.name: Hilltop Fort Rajasthan
south_asia.summary: A Rajasthan hill fort is a classic high-control stronghold with excellent wall geometry, but water and heat stress define whether it thrives or slowly fails.

southeast_asia.name: Palawan
southeast_asia.summary: Palawan is a large island system that balances isolation, defensibility, and resource diversity. It works when distributed settlements and logistics are coordinated at island-wide scale. You die when governance fractures and shipping disruption desynchronizes regional supply.

southeast_asia.name: Rice Terrace Highlands
southeast_asia.summary: Rice Terrace Highlands are elevated agrarian settlements with built-in food potential. They work by combining controllable approach routes with reliable staple production systems. You die when irrigation, labor coordination, or slope access fails during stress cycles.

southeast_asia.name: Banda Neira
southeast_asia.summary: A small island settlement with strong maritime separation, historic fortifications, and access to coastal resources. It works best as a low-profile island refuge, but limited scale and supply dependence cap long-term resilience.

uk_ireland.name: Lindisfarne
uk_ireland.summary: A tidal island with natural separation, limited access windows, and a defensible settlement pattern. It works well for a disciplined small group, but tide dependency and resource limits cap long-term resilience.

western_europe.name: Mont Saint-Michel
western_europe.summary: Mont Saint-Michel is one of the hardest micro-sites to assault thanks to tidal separation; what kills you here is throughput limits in food, space, and medical response.

western_europe.name: Heligoland
western_europe.summary: Heligoland is one of the strongest isolation plays in Western Europe: remote, compact, and easier to monitor than mainland sites. What kills you here is maritime dependency when weather or fuel cuts the lifeline.

western_europe.name: Carcassonne
western_europe.summary: Carcassonne is a premier fortified shell with layered walls and command depth; what kills you here is sustainment fatigue behind intact defenses.

industrial_site.name: Itaipu Dam
industrial_site.summary: Itaipu Dam has exceptional energy potential and water access, making it operationally powerful, but its scale and strategic value make defense extremely demanding.

industrial_site.name: Murmansk Icebreaker Port
industrial_site.summary: A polar maritime hub with specialist icebreaker infrastructure and Arctic access. However, port exposure, supply dependency, and harsh operating conditions limit long-term security.

institutional_compound.summary: Hanle Observatory is an isolation-dominant survival option with low encounter pressure, but extreme altitude and remoteness impose severe physiological and logistics penalties.

institutional_compound.name: 2e REP Barracks (Calvi)
institutional_compound.summary: 2e REP Calvi is a hard military compound with disciplined layout and perimeter control, but it sits on a populated island with finite local capacity. What kills you here is prolonged resupply failure after the initial defensive advantage burns off.

institutional_compound.name: Area 51
institutional_compound.summary: Area 51 combines remoteness, controlled approaches, and hardened infrastructure, but its dominant failure mode is systems complexity debt: without specialized maintenance pipelines, high-tech capabilities decay into unusable overhead.

landmark_structure.summary: Hormuz lighthouse has useful separation and surveillance value, but what kills you here is capacity exhaustion: the site is too small and too harsh to sustain a community once short-term stores are depleted.

landmark_structure.name: Phu Quoc Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: A coastal lighthouse with visibility, limited access, and some island separation. It offers short-term observation value, but exposure, lack of resources, and dependence on nearby settlement make it weak as a base.

landmark_structure.name: Cape Point Lighthouse
landmark_structure.summary: Cape Point Lighthouse has tactical lookout value and some geographic separation, but it lacks the carrying capacity and resource depth needed for sustained habitation. It works best as an observation and signaling outpost rather than a primary survival settlement.
